about: Patterns proved by four delivered projects, stripped of their business domains on purpose. Node types: pattern | libraryGap | kbDoc | libraryDoc | source. Edge types: explained_in | documented_in | seen_in | corrects. The graph is an index — the prose document named in kbDoc explains why a rule exists.

sources.A: 433 pages · 163 CRUDs · 619 rules · 22 studio consoles · 27 schedulers

convention.evidence: evidenceCount = how many of the four deliveries showed it. 1 is an idea, 2 a lead, 3+ a convention you should follow. evidenceCount: null with attribution: "unrecorded" means the technique was read out of a delivery but which one was not recorded — treat the RULE as sound and the WEIGHT as unknown; it is never a claim that no delivery showed it.

nodes.name: One `<Screen> Screen Data (Studio)` rule returns the whole page
nodes.rule: Each studio console's load() makes exactly ONE ctx.callRule that returns every list, the capability flags, the resolved locale and a diagnostic trace in one map, with each list wrapped in a `safe { }` closure that records its exception into `__trace` so an empty dropdown can be told apart from a read that quietly threw.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.rules[] EXECUTION_RULE named `<Screen> Screen Data (Studio)`, called from the studio component's `load()`
nodes.antiPattern: One fetch per widget. The screen then has N failure modes, N loading states, and no single place to enforce the row scope — and a failed read renders as an empty list indistinguishable from no data.

nodes.name: Server-resolved capability flags that report WHICH mechanism decided
nodes.rule: A `<Screen> Rights (Studio)` rule probes the platform role API, detects that it is fail-closed (`platformUsable = apiAnswered && (isAdmin || probe.any{k,v->v})`), falls back to a project-side `system_settings` jsonb store, and returns `[canEdit, canDelete, decidedBy, degraded, probe, via, scope, scopeWhy]` so a wrong answer is debuggable from the browser; the command rule re-checks the same resolver server-side regardless.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.rules[] EXECUTION_RULE; project-side fallback keys in a `system_settings` jsonb table (`tasks.role_members`, `tasks.see_all_users`, `tasks.<kind>_users`)
nodes.antiPattern: `hasAnyRoleGroup` answering false for a user in nine role groups without throwing, then a fail-open loop over role names written to work around it. Three modules chased this before anyone grepped for the existing resolver — the answer was already in a comment older than the change request.

nodes.name: Row-level data localization via a `*Loc` side channel
nodes.rule: Business rows carry a `localized` jsonb column; ONE dynamic CRUD (`app_localized_cruid`, 37 SQL methods, each `SELECT id AS row_id, CAST(localized AS text) AS loc FROM <table> WHERE localized IS NOT NULL`) exposes them as `<entity>Loc` keys on the screen payload, and the client merges by naming convention (`suppliersLoc` → `d.suppliers`) — then warns aloud on the console when every `*Loc` came back empty rather than degrading silently into the base locale.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json one CRUD with N `methodType:"SQL"` methods named `<entity>Loc`, `returnsArray:false`; author JS helper `appApplyLoc`
nodes.antiPattern: Testing `Array.isArray()` on the side channel: the `*Loc` producers declare `returnsArray:false`, so a single-row channel arrives as a bare object and exactly the rows that needed repairing were skipped.

nodes.name: Two-way `data-en`/`data-hy` label swap that edits text nodes, not subtrees
nodes.rule: Every static label in a studio component carries BOTH `data-en` and `data-hy`, and one `applyLocale()` swaps them in either direction by rewriting the element's own child text nodes — never `el.textContent =`, because that is a subtree delete wearing a string assignment.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin `properties.html` (paired attributes) + the component's script
nodes.antiPattern: Two real bugs in one routine: (1) `return` when the locale is not the second language and overwrite the base text with no copy kept — a switch back leaves every label stranded; (2) `el.textContent = t` on a `<label>` that wraps a required-marker `<span>` deletes the marker on first draw. One such marker never rendered once in eleven modules.

nodes.name: A cron chain, not BPMN, is the process engine
nodes.rule: 27 schedulers, each `actionType: RUN_RULE` with a `job.explanation` citing the requirement it implements ("A-19 daily 05:00") and cron minute offsets that encode the dependency order — 02:00 KPI aggregation → 02:10 allocate shared costs → 02:25 rebuild cash ledger → 02:30 economics → 02:35 value inventory → 02:40 cash-flow projection → 02:45 close period → 02:50 break-even.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.schedulers[] `{actionType:"RUN_RULE", job:{expression, explanation}, actionRuleIdentifier}` → an EXECUTION_RULE per job
nodes.antiPattern: Drawing five business workflows — one per document lifecycle — and deploying none. `grep 'service.workflow.start'` over all 619 rules returns nothing; the only start action sits on a page called `Branches`. Also: all 27 schedulers ship `enabled: true`, so importing the export starts a 5-minute polling watchdog and an 02:45 period close the same night.

nodes.name: A vendored studio library shared by every component
nodes.rule: One JS_CLASSIC file at `tenant-files/studio/app-kit/app-kit.js`, declared as `libs:[{name:"appkit", globalVar:"appkit", assets:[{kind:"JS_CLASSIC", path:"studio/app-kit/app-kit.js"}]}]` and reached as `ctx.libs.appkit` — so cross-cutting behaviour exists once instead of once per screen.
nodes.artefact: tenant-files/studio/<kit>/<kit>.js + studioModel.libs[] + per-script `libNames`
nodes.antiPattern: THE project's biggest avoidable cost: app-kit carries ONLY the breadcrumb proxy. `errText` is duplicated in 24/24 scripts, `applyLocale`/`say`/`bind`/`esc` in 23/24, the `ctx.callRule` logging prelude in 19/24. One component's CSS literally opens "shared A screen kit, copied from the documents console". Every cross-cutting fix became a 22-to-24-place sweep.

nodes.name: Promote in-body action buttons into the breadcrumb by DOM proxy
nodes.rule: Rather than rewriting fourteen screens' buttons, the shared kit mirrors each live DOM button into a `ctx.breadcrumb` descriptor and forwards the click, tracking label and enabled state with a MutationObserver — and resolves the breadcrumb spinner on the FIRST `disabled` change after the click, never by re-reading the final state.
nodes.artefact: tenant-files studio library + the `ctx.breadcrumb` API
nodes.antiPattern: Reading `el.disabled` inside the MutationObserver callback: deleting the last row re-enables and re-disables in ONE synchronous block, so the callback sees `true`, never resolves, and the block-panel overlay covers the whole screen for the full timeout.

nodes.name: Every command button goes through one `action()` helper
nodes.rule: `action(btnSel, msgSel, rule, input, after)` owns the in-flight guard (`busy`), the button disable, and the message lifecycle — the strip is cleared BEFORE the call so a failed render leaves it empty rather than wrong, and the success sentence is re-asserted AFTER `after()` so a reload cannot leave the previous message standing.
nodes.artefact: author JS inside nct.html.plugin studioModel.scripts[].code
nodes.antiPattern: Dropping a click that arrives while a load() is in flight with no message and no button state — the PREVIOUS action's success text stays on screen and reads exactly like the new one succeeded. Five sightings, the worst being an operator seeing a database error after a stock receipt had actually succeeded, whose obvious reaction is to retry and double-receive.

nodes.name: `chart.js.plugin` nodes as children of a studio component, addressed by `<plugin>` tags
nodes.rule:
The studio component supplies the grid, cards and KPI strip; the platform chart plugin supplies the canvas and query binding — `
` addresses a real chart node that is a CHILD of the html node.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin (studioModel) with chart.js.plugin children + `<plugin id name>` tags in its `properties.html`
nodes.antiPattern: Hanging charts directly off `parsis` with no layout between them — they stack full-width with no card, heading or row. `validate` flags it twice in this project, on the two legacy chart pages.

nodes.name: Instrument every server call by wrapping `ctx.callRule` once
nodes.rule: A self-installing prelude rebinds `ctx.callRule` to time the call, inject the reading locale (`input.__loc`), and write an info/error row to a `ui_event_log` table on resolve or reject — guarded by `ctx.__ghLogWrapped` for re-mount idempotence and by an explicit skip so the logger never logs itself.
nodes.artefact: author JS prelude + an EXECUTION_RULE `Log UI Event (Studio)` + a plain log table with its own CRUD
nodes.antiPattern: Forgetting `if (action === 'Log UI Event (Studio)' || action === 'Logs Screen Data (Studio)') return;` — the log table fills with itself.

nodes.name: One `css.byTheme["*"]` block for all five skins, tiny per-skin blocks for status hues only
nodes.rule: Declare every colour as `var(--platform-token, <light literal>)` — the four dark skins define `--background`/`--current-line`/`--foreground`/`--comment` on `:root` and the light skin does not, so one block resolves correctly on all five; then override ONLY the status colours per dark skin, with measured ≥4.5:1 values, because the platform palette collapses green/cyan/purple to nearly one hue on some skins.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.css.byTheme
nodes.antiPattern: Bare colour literals in the `*` block (validate WARNs on these), and undefined custom properties — one module used five token names that do not exist (`--app-line`, `--app-ink`, `--app-sunk`) and an undefined custom property invalidates the whole declaration, so the control rendered unstyled.

nodes.name: An error formatter that refuses to present an identity hash as an explanation
nodes.rule: A server executor failure arrives as an object with no enumerable fields whose only stringification is `…ExecuteResponse$ExecutionError@5e20cfdf`; the formatter detects that shape, says "the rule failed without returning a message — check the server log", and keeps the hash as the correlation token tying a screenshot to a log line.
nodes.artefact: author JS helper (belongs in the shared kit)
nodes.antiPattern: Printing `String(e)` and showing an operator a memory address. Also: fixing it on the one screen you happened to open — a later sweep found three distinct error shapes across 22 screens, where anchoring on one body would have covered 4 and silently missed 18.

nodes.name: Classify every entity as register / document / ledger / queue before choosing an artefact
nodes.rule: Registers (a few dozen code lists plus the master tables) get crud.table + a form group; documents (header+lines — `document`→`document_line`, `case`→`task`, `run`→`stop`) get a studio console over a header CRUD and its line CRUDs; ledgers (`item`/`item_movement`, `account`/`account_movement`) get an append-only movement table plus a balance and a named rule per direction; queues (`task`, `alert`, `inbox`, `exception`) get a filterable console board, never a report.
nodes.artefact: the whole export — dynamic-cruds.json + the page tree + which plugin each page carries
nodes.antiPattern: Treating a queue as a report. The PRD is explicit: "the compliance dashboard is a work queue, not a report. Each open gate is clickable and closable. This is why it cannot be delegated to a BI tool."

nodes.name: A quantity that starts moving creates an obligation on every path that reverses it
nodes.rule: When a module makes a balance move in a direction nothing moved it before, enumerate every flow that reverses, cancels or partially undoes that movement and state for each whether it was updated or deliberately left — in the module that adds the FORWARD movement, not the one that eventually finds the gap.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULEs over an append-only movement table plus a balance column
nodes.antiPattern: "Record Delivery Rejection had always returned no stock, and had always been correct to, because nothing had ever removed any." One forward change silently broke a rule written years earlier and touched by nobody; every existing assertion about rejection concerned the credit note and the order status, both of which stayed right.

nodes.name: Seed data written from the spec agrees with the spec and proves nothing
nodes.rule: A balance is verified by causing a movement and re-reading it, never by inspecting a value that agrees with expectations; where a test cannot execute the rule it asserts on the rule's TEXT that the write exists, and a module claiming to move stock ends with an assertion that the balance update is present, not merely the ledger insert.
nodes.artefact: project-db.dump rows vs rep-objects.rules[] scripts
nodes.antiPattern: The mirror error: deriving STRUCTURE from seed text. Three free-text values in an `inventory.location` column were promoted into three warehouse entities; two were storage rooms and the third was a state ("Quarantine bay"), and "a dimension whose members are not the same kind of thing is not a dimension." The subdivision turned out not to be wanted at all.

nodes.name: Making a list editable moves its meaning onto the row
nodes.rule: Before opening a closed enum to editing, enumerate every branch that compares against its literal members and turn each into a COLUMN on the row, filled in when a value is created, with the create form asking for it in the user's words — otherwise value number four silently takes whatever the `else` branch happens to do.
nodes.artefact: a code-list (dimension) table whose columns encode consequences, plus the create form beside the picker
nodes.antiPattern: "Both defaults are the dangerous one, and neither was ever chosen." Produce nobody grew would back an own-grown provenance claim on the say-so of a string comparison that missed.

nodes.name: For every list a screen reads, name the rule that WRITES it
nodes.rule: A fixture is a decision about who creates the row, made silently — nine rounds of scenario testing passed over a table the application could not write, because every acceptance test began "given a stock item…". Where the create rule does not exist the feature is incomplete however well the screen behaves; where it does, the create path belongs beside the picker that failed to offer the row, not only in a header.
nodes.artefact: an inline door button next to every `<select>` in a studio component + the list page it opens
nodes.antiPattern: Every list a screen reads sourced from seed data with no create path anywhere. Invisible to offline validate, to every screen suite, and to nine rounds of testing, because all of them supplied the row as a fixture.

nodes.name: NEGATIVE — never file the business app inside the `Pages` authoring drawer
nodes.rule: A ships all 21 business screens as a sub-group named `A` INSIDE `Pages`, one level deeper than the fourteen admin console links; `Home` is duplicated as `Dashboard` in that sub-group (same content identifier `34c97297-…`); `Library > Platform` holds Branches/Ontology/Profile/Queries/Sources; every sub-heading is also a link to its first child (validate reports 11 duplicate targets); and 38 code-list registers sit in the sidebar.
nodes.artefact: branch.virtualPlugins[] name="Nct left nav" → content.properties.modelGroups.stringValue
nodes.antiPattern: This IS the anti-pattern. The remedy is three commands: `quicklink rm --label Home`, move the business pages into business-named TOP-level groups in the PRD's own words, and drop the Platform sub-group. What the project got RIGHT and is worth copying: all 173 items carry an item-level `localizedMap.name.hy_AM` AND all 171 links carry the inner `linkModel.localizedMap` copy too — the exact pairing doc 17 demands.

nodes.name: NEGATIVE — Groovy capability flags without matching page/nav roleAccess
nodes.rule: The PRD carries a full 8-role permission matrix; the export gates 367 pages with the baseline `Author` group, 5 with role groups from a DIFFERENT project's starter template, and exactly ONE with a business role — so every persona sees all 171 nav links and can reach every page by URL, while all real gating lives in Groovy.
nodes.artefact: siteMapPage.roleAccess.roleGroupAccessors + PageModel.roleAccess in the nav modelGroups
nodes.antiPattern: Gating in Groovy only. The data is safe; the product still tells an operator it is a system for somebody else. And sweep the starter template: five role groups and three virtual plugins left over from the template's own domain are still in the nav.

nodes.name: NEGATIVE — 163 generated CRUDs, only the ~22 the consoles use ever finished
nodes.rule: `mrjun.py validate` finds 71 form actions with no `onBeforeCompleteRuleIdentifier` (the form submits and saves nothing), 63 delete methods that physically DELETE from FK-referenced tables, 131 method/query script divergences, 126 methods with `queryIdentifier` unset, 38 form groups pointing at the shared system Landing page, and 11 methods with untyped `OFFSET (:pageNumber * :rowsInPage)` that work from the UI table and fail from a rule.
nodes.artefact: crud.table.plugin `properties.model` createActions/editActions + dynamic-cruds.json methods
nodes.antiPattern: It breaks doc 24 §1.2's own justification for keeping the boring pages — "if the component breaks, the boring page still runs the business" is NOT true when most of those pages cannot write. Either finish them or do not generate them.

nodes.name: A module closing a defect class enumerates the surface programmatically and asserts over it
nodes.rule: Anchoring a sweep on an identifier ("the script named main", "the function named fillSelects", "the four screens that happened to be open") is not a sweep — a screen is the union of its scripts, and source order is not visibility; walk every script on every component and end with an assertion over that enumeration so the next instance fails the build.
nodes.artefact: a build-time scan over branches.json → nct.html.plugin → studioModel.scripts[]
nodes.antiPattern: Also: an assertion that states only what it FORBIDS returns empty and reports success. A sweep looking for a CRUD alias in `properties.model.stringValue` found none on any FORM page — where it lives eight levels down in `properties.settings` — and reported every Add button correctly wired while ten opened another table's form. "A scan that finds no matches is evidence about the scan, not about the tree, until something proves the scan can find a match at all."

nodes.name: Whatever enforces a screen's rules is called once at the end of `load()`
nodes.rule: A screen's mount state is a state and something has to set it: if the function that decides which fields are live is only reached from events, the form opens in the markup's authored state and only becomes correct once the operator touches something — and a suite that tests contextual behaviour must assert at mount, before it clicks anything.
nodes.artefact: the studio component's `load()` / `main` script
nodes.antiPattern: The same shape as authoring a panel hidden in the markup with nothing un-hiding it at init — the raw-material side of a screen opened blank for four modules. Markup carries a starting state, the script carries the rules that govern it, and if the script only runs on an event the two disagree until the operator acts.

nodes.name: A disabled control and a rule that refuses are not two safeguards
nodes.rule: Before disabling a control, find the rule that already refuses the thing; if one exists delete the disable and let the refusal speak, because the greyed control states the conclusion and withholds the reason, can drift from the rule without anything failing, and only governs the one screen that draws it.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE guard vs. author JS `el.disabled`
nodes.antiPattern: The marker class that marked nothing: `wh-off` was applied to "make the shape of each movement legible from one screen" and had no CSS rule anywhere in the project. Four modules carried it and cited it in their own justification; all anyone ever saw was the browser's default greying.

nodes.name: A seam between two modules is a requirement, not an implementation detail
nodes.rule: Testing found the failures were at the handoffs, not the steps — QC→warehouse (two inventory ledgers with no bridge), QC→plan (archived batches still feeding output totals), equipment→tasks (a task generated from a machine reported nothing back), invoice→cash (a receipt reduced receivables and never credited cash) — so where a core loop names a handoff, an acceptance criterion must exercise BOTH sides of it.
nodes.artefact: the plan/acceptance criteria, and the rule pairs that write both sides
nodes.antiPattern: "One module writing half of a two-sided fact, two modules disagreeing about the same number, a rule storing a value no screen can display." The principal risk was named as building outward before the core loop closes; what actually happened is that the core loop was sound and the seams were not.

nodes.name: Five-tier CRUD method vocabulary
nodes.rule: 480 methods across 38 CRUDs use only ~30 distinct names, tiered as base-8 / register / header+lines kit / lifecycle verbs / derivation / domain, so any CRUD's capability is readable from its method list alone.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json methods[]
nodes.antiPattern: Ad-hoc per-entity verb naming; here the underscore in _deleteHeader deliberately marks an internal primitive the UI must never call.

nodes.name: Header+lines aggregate CRUD with Map/JsonNode coercion prelude
nodes.rule: create/update/delete are GROOVY orchestrators over SQL primitives so a form can POST one nested object; a fixed prelude of _size/_at/_num/_txt/_ref/_lineNo/_fk closures absorbs the fact that line payloads arrive as Groovy Maps or Jackson JsonNodes depending on caller.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json GROOVY methods create/update/delete
nodes.antiPattern: update runs deleteLines(id) then re-inserts every line, so line ids churn on each save and any stock_movement.doc_line_id written earlier dangles; a diff-based upsert keyed on line_number would cost little.

nodes.name: Twelve-step posting-engine rule skeleton
nodes.rule: Every posting rule runs the same order: helper closures, actor, multi-source subject resolution, load+null guard, status guard, role guard, period-lock guard, business preconditions, derive via stamp*/compute*/recompute*, re-read and sanity-check, write stock_movement, flip status LAST via a guarded transition, then audit.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json rules[] ruleType=EXECUTION_RULE
nodes.antiPattern: Flipping status before writing the ledger. A lifecycle wrapper comment records it explicitly: 'Calling post() here instead would flip the status and move nothing.'

nodes.name: Status transition guarded in the WHERE clause
nodes.rule: post/approve methods are UPDATE … SET status='POSTED' … WHERE id = CAST(:id AS uuid) AND status = 'SUBMITTED', so a double-post is a zero-row no-op instead of a corruption.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json SQL methods post/approve/submit/reject
nodes.antiPattern: A blind UPDATE … WHERE id = :id, which lets a retried click re-post an already-posted document.

nodes.name: One ref_label table holds every enum, fully localised
nodes.rule: A single register with vocabulary/code/label/localized-jsonb/sort_order/color carries all 30 enumerations (144 codes, 144/144 translated); every dropdown is then a two-line rule calling service.global.conversion.toSelectOptionsLocalized(list,'code','label').
nodes.artefact: a `<schema>.ref_label` table + rules bucketed '<project>/04_rules · choices'
nodes.antiPattern: The crud.table.plugin status columns ignore it and inline their own enumValues with a single-language displayName — 112/112 columns show default-locale status text under headers rendered in the other two locales.

nodes.name: Fully localised shared left nav with a role-denied console group
nodes.rule: The rendering nav is one shared virtual plugin; ten business groups each carry a group-level localizedMap for name and icon, all 55 leaves are trilingual, Home sits in a business group, and the authoring 'Pages' group is deliberately empty-localised and carries roleAccess view:false for every business role, repeated on each child.
nodes.artefact: site.kicker.plugin properties.modelGroups.stringValue → pagesModel[]
nodes.antiPattern: Per-page site.kicker nodes carry a stale 1512-byte copy of modelGroups that renders nowhere — never hand-edit them.

nodes.name: A page of PRD arithmetic compiled into one derivation statement
nodes.rule: A single derive method turns six typed measurements into fourteen derived columns in one UPDATE — the multiplier, two areas, two separately modelled loss sources, planned vs actual vs abnormal loss, and a `surplus_requires_approval` flag against a tolerance parameter.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json cutMarker.computeMarker / stampConversion (SQL)
nodes.antiPattern: Letting the form write derived columns. The posting rule sequences stampLines → stampConversion → computeMarker → recomputeSizes, re-reads, then validates the result is non-empty before posting.

nodes.name: Server-side snapshot stamping so history cannot be rewritten
nodes.rule: stampLines copies the item code, the variant code and the full document-specific item name onto every line and costs it at the source unit's own `unit_cost` via a COALESCE chain (transfer line → roll → existing), all in SQL at post time, so a later rename cannot change a historical report.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json <doc>.stampLines (SQL)
nodes.antiPattern: Typing the snapshot values into the form, or resolving them at read time by joining live reference data.

nodes.name: Control equation as live columns settled by deltas
nodes.rule: The source document's line carries qty / qty_used / qty_returned / qty_lost / qty_open, and each downstream document's post rule calls settleLine with exactly one non-empty delta; a header refreshSettlement then rolls it up to OPEN/PARTIALLY_SETTLED/CLOSED within tolerance.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json materialTransfer.settleLine (SQL)
nodes.antiPattern: Recomputing the balance by aggregating downstream documents at close time — slower, and it cannot flag a per-line tolerance breach the way flagVariances does per UOM (0.150 KG / 0.500 M).

nodes.name: XOR gateway on a computed balance, defaulting to rework
nodes.rule: A service task recomputes the control equation, an exclusive gateway with default=unbalanced routes back to the allocation user task, and only the predicate-guarded balanced flow reaches approval and posting — the 'cannot close while quantities are unaccounted for' rule expressed as a loop, not an error toast.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json workflows[].bpmnContent + elements[]
nodes.antiPattern: Making the safe branch the default. Here default="Flow_unbalanced" means a predicate failure loops rather than escaping to approval.

nodes.name: Gate / persist / lifecycle / engine rule layering
nodes.rule: Per document: a one-line PREDICATE reading status decides whether the button renders, a two-line persist rule handles form submit, a thin lifecycle wrapper re-checks the guard server-side and delegates by name, and the fat starred engine does the work.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json rules[].description prefixed 'aas/04_rules · <bucket> ·'
nodes.antiPattern: Rules are invoked by display name — service.rule("Անցկացնել փաստացի ծախսը") — so a studio rename breaks every caller with no static check and no error until the button is clicked.

nodes.name: State machine rendered as predicate-gated direct row actions
nodes.rule: The list table's editActions carry Submit/Post/Reject/Reverse/Print/Correct as direct:true actions (no form — click runs the rule on the selected row), each with a predicateIdentifier controlling visibility and an onBeforeCompleteRuleIdentifier doing the work, all trilingual in both localizedNames and localizedButtonNames.
nodes.artefact: crud.table.plugin properties.model.stringValue → editActions.actions[]
nodes.antiPattern: Putting lifecycle transitions inside the edit form, which forces a save to change state and lets a user edit a posted document on the way.

nodes.name: Reports as three-method CRUDs over a SELECT
nodes.rule: A report is a dynamic CRUD with no backing table and exactly find/findAll/count, where findAll is a plain SQL SELECT (often UNION ALL across two tracking modes with a discriminator column) and dtoFields declares the camelCase shape — inheriting the table plugin, filter bar, column localisation and paging for free.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json rpt* CRUDs (3 methods, dtoFields)
nodes.antiPattern: An id column is mandatory even when nothing links out — the table plugin keys rows on it, so r.id / l.id are selected purely to satisfy it.

nodes.name: Every PRD tunable becomes an app_setting row read at runtime
nodes.rule: A categorised key/value/value_type register holds tolerances, the period lock, approval thresholds, notification recipient lists, label dimensions and company details, and a shared SETTING closure in every rule reads it — so an administrator tunes policy without a developer.
nodes.artefact: `<schema>.app_setting` + the SETTING/cfg closure in rules
nodes.antiPattern: Rows nothing reads. The 12 doc.prefix.* rows are dead — all 17 prefixes are hardcoded in createHeader SQL, and five have no matching row at all.

nodes.name: Per-locale mail templates plus per-locale recipient lists, dispatched in one loop
nodes.rule: A mailTemplate has no locale slot, so make three (alias, aliasEn, aliasRu) and three recipient settings (key, key.en, key.ru), then loop for (sfx in ['','Ru','En']) skipping any locale whose recipient list is empty — disabling a language is clearing a settings row, not editing code.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json mailTemplates[] + the PDF/mail EXECUTION_RULEs
nodes.antiPattern: An unguarded service.report.pdf.email call: renderAttachments runs BEFORE the send and rethrows, so a PDF-service outage loses the notification too. Catch and fall back to service.notification.mail.

nodes.name: Transliterate non-Latin text before it reaches a PDF cell
nodes.rule: The pdfme font cannot render the project's script, so every PDF rule carries a ~40-entry character map plus a digraph pass applied first, and a cn(code,name) helper enforces 'code · transliterated-name' as the only shape allowed into a cell.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json rules whose description starts 'Renders pdf…'
nodes.antiPattern: Running the per-character map before the digraph map, which turns ու into vo.

nodes.name: «Modify the document» opens a correcting version that reverses and re-enters
nodes.rule: An approved document is never edited: a button opens a revision-numbered correction row, one-open-at-a-time enforced, with an empty (not placeholder) reason that the approve rule refuses until it is ≥10 chars and not the prompt itself; approving runs the existing reversal machinery so the ledger really moves and both versions survive.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json documentCorrection.openForDocument (SQL) + the ⭐ v1.2 §9 rules
nodes.antiPattern: A pre-filled 'fill in the reason' placeholder — the rule comment records that it is 52 chars long and so satisfies both the non-empty and the length check, letting a director approve a correction whose stated reason is an instruction to state a reason.

nodes.name: FIFO suggestion stored as data, with the shortfall, so the override is auditable
nodes.rule: JOIN LATERAL … ORDER BY creation_time LIMIT 1 writes `suggested_unit_id` and `shortfall_qty` onto each request line in one statement, and a companion fifoQueue returns the ordered queue with ROW_NUMBER() AS fifo_position so the approver sees what he is overriding.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json materialRequest.suggestFifoRolls (SQL)
nodes.antiPattern: Computing the suggestion in the UI. Note also that cost_finalized = true sits in the eligibility filter, so the 'un-costed stock cannot move' rule is enforced in the suggestion, not only in validation.

nodes.name: Charts themed through CSS custom properties read at render time
nodes.rule: cssByTheme declares one palette per theme (* for light, then each dark theme) as --c1..--c8 / --c-good/warn/risk/crit / --r1..--r4, and the chart JS reads them via getComputedStyle with literal fallbacks, using transparent paper_bgcolor/plot_bgcolor and font.color: cs.color so one definition reads correctly in five themes.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin properties.Javascript.stringValue
nodes.antiPattern: A chart has no per-locale slot at all — a unit suffix in the default locale is baked into the JS, so all 31 charts render that locale's units under every other locale.

nodes.name: Description field as a grep-able index back to the PRD
nodes.rule: Every rule, workflow, process group, mail and PDF template carries a description of the form 'aas/<step>_<kind> · <bucket> · <detail>' or a PRD clause citation, with ⭐ marking the seven rules that implement a named requirement and must not be casually edited.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json *.description
nodes.antiPattern: Queries (439), forms (32) and formGroups (32) carry no description at all, so the convention stops exactly where the volume is highest.

nodes.name: Strict list / form-landing / form page triple per entity
nodes.rule: Each business entity gets exactly <entity-plural>, <entity>-forms and form-<entity> (plus form-<entity>-review where an approval exists), with only the list appearing in the nav — 55 nav leaves cover 129 pages.
nodes.artefact: siteMapPage alias convention + the 5 page archetypes
nodes.antiPattern: The page tree is flat — every list is a direct child of Home rather than nested under its nav group, so the tree and the nav disagree about structure.

nodes.name: Status sets as CHECK constraints, not Postgres enum types
nodes.rule: 66 CHECK constraints of the form CHECK (col::text = ANY (ARRAY['DRAFT','SUBMITTED','POSTED',…])) keep the DB honest even if a rule is bypassed, while staying alterable with a plain ALTER TABLE and pairing with ref_label for labels, ordering and colour.
nodes.artefact: project-db.dump schemas[].checkConstraints
nodes.antiPattern: uniqueConstraints is 0 — nothing prevents a duplicate doc_no, and document numbers are random hex (gen_random_uuid substring) rather than a gapless sequence.

nodes.name: Bilingual error messages that name the current state
nodes.rule: Every operator-facing throw is 'native / English' slash-separated and includes the actual value that failed, e.g. 'Only a SUBMITTED document can be posted (current: ' + doc.status + ')'.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json rules[] ruleScriptStr
nodes.antiPattern: Stating only the required state. Also note the CALL wrapper walks the cause chain with a guard++ < 12 bound because a self-referencing cause otherwise hangs the request.

nodes.name: Inline help that explains the interaction model, not the field
nodes.rule: 78 nct.help.plugin nodes, 78 fully trilingual, teaching how the screen works rather than restating the label — e.g. 'Status is not typed in — it is the document's history. It moves with the register buttons: Submit, Approve, Reject, Mark as fulfilled, Cancel.'
nodes.artefact: nct.help.plugin properties.helpSettings.stringValue → localizedMap.message
nodes.antiPattern: Help text that restates the field label ('Enter the status'), or help authored in the default locale only — which makes the one paragraph that teaches the screen the single monolingual thing on it.

nodes.name: Claim column: idempotent workflow start from both a user action and a scheduler
nodes.rule: Give every subject table a `<x>_process_identifier` column; a person's action starts the process only when it is empty, a scheduler starts it via a conditional `UPDATE … SET col='CLAIMING' WHERE col IS NULL RETURNING *` whose null return means somebody else won, then both write the real process id back with a method that only accepts `IS NULL OR 'CLAIMING'`.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-CRUD SQL method + EXECUTION_RULE calling service.workflow.start
nodes.antiPattern: Guarding only on the Groovy side (read the row, check the column, start): two scheduler ticks or a double-click both pass the check and open two processes. The claim must be one conditional UPDATE that returns the row.

nodes.name: Every statutory number is a row, computed in working days
nodes.rule: Model clocks as a `deadline_policy` CRUD (`code`, `durationValue`, `durationUnit` in MINUTES/HOURS/CALENDAR_DAYS/WORKING_DAYS/MONTHS, `escalationPoints`, `ownerRole`, `approvalState`), resolve with `applyPolicy(code, from, holidays)` over a business-maintained holiday table, compose the code from state (`'CONTAINMENT_' + priority`), and throw — never default — when the row is missing.
nodes.artefact: reference CRUD + Groovy closure prelude
nodes.antiPattern: `from.plusDays(3)` for "three working days", and `policyValue(code, 24)` silently defaulting when Compliance never configured the row — the deadline is then wrong and nobody knows whose number it is.

nodes.name: Row-level scope on the table's find rule, written last, failing closed
nodes.rule: Wire a `findRuleIdentifier` per CRUD table that rebuilds the filter map from `attrs` (Jackson nodes, including rowsInPage/pageNumber), then appends the caller's scope AFTER the forwarded values so a client-supplied value cannot widen it; an unknown user resolves to an impossible UUID, not to "all".
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE bound as crud.table.plugin model.findRuleIdentifier
nodes.antiPattern: Reading `param` instead of `attrs` (empty outside a delegated CRUD method, so the filter form, column filters and paging all silently vanish), returning unscoped rows when the staff lookup finds nothing, or scoping the table but not the Export action.

nodes.name: _subject(alias): one form group served by both a table row action and a BPMN user task
nodes.rule: Resolve the subject by `context.data.getAttr(alias+'Id')` then `subjectId`, fall back to the context CRUD row, then overlay every attr whose key names a field of the row — so the same form group works from a register row (values on the row, attrs empty) and from a user task (row unseeded, values in attrs).
nodes.artefact: Groovy closure in EXECUTION_RULEs behind formGroup actions
nodes.antiPattern: Building two form groups — a "table" one and a "task" one — for the same action, then having them drift.

nodes.name: Separation of duties checked on two identities, at instance level, as a predicate
nodes.rule: Make the approve/decline row action's `predicateIdentifier` a rule that refuses the proposer AND the case owner on that specific case (not just the role), reads the current state from the DB rather than a form copy, and returns false on every unknown; the button then simply is not rendered for the wrong person.
nodes.artefact: PREDICATE rule on a crud.table.plugin action and a BPMN gateway
nodes.antiPattern: Relying on role separation alone ("only the approver role may approve") — the case owner who also holds that role approves their own case; and reading `isHighRisk` from the submitted row instead of re-fetching it.

nodes.name: KPI tile: value and comparison from one query, two replacements
nodes.rule: A Plotly `indicator` in `mode:'number+delta'` bound to two replacements over the SAME query identifier pulling different `columnName`s (`value`, `prev`), height 118px, transparent paper/plot, font colour from `getComputedStyle(el).color`, and delta colours set to the metric's own polarity.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin (Plotly engine) + one query, two QUERY replacements
nodes.antiPattern: Two separate queries for current and previous — they drift under a filter change; and leaving `increasing:{color:'green'}` on a KPI where rising is bad (open cases, net loss, overdue requests).

nodes.name: Cross-filter on the dimension the chart groups by
nodes.rule: End the chart JS with `cfg.options.onClick = function(e,els){ … this.crossFilter('<Param>', v); }.bind(this)` plus an `onHover` pointer cursor, and always pass the parameter that matches the chart's own GROUP BY, so a click narrows the whole board coherently.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin JS + global.replacement.plugin filter bar
nodes.antiPattern: Cross-filtering a parameter the chart does not group by (clicking a bar then filters away the bar you clicked), or wiring click handlers on some charts and not others so the board feels broken.

nodes.name: One dashboard per numbered report requirement, all the same shape
nodes.rule: Turn the PRD's report table into N pages, each a `global.replacement.plugin` filter bar + a 4-tile KPI row + 6-7 charts in Bootstrap cards, chart titles supplied by `nct.label.plugin` nodes whose id is `hdr_` + the chart's own UUID, and titles written as findings ("Why proposals are declined") not column names.
nodes.artefact: siteMapPage + global.replacement.plugin + chart.js.plugin grid
nodes.antiPattern: One giant 30-chart dashboard with no owner and no requirement id behind it — nobody can say which chart is allowed to be removed.

nodes.name: The workbench: one page, one tab plugin, one filter+table pair per child entity
nodes.rule: For an aggregate whose children are registers rather than line grids, build a single page with `nct.tab.plugin` whose `tabModel.items[i]` binds to child parsis node `i` BY ORDER, each child holding exactly `dynaform.filter.form.plugin` (fields in a `filter-row` html as fcell1..N + fcellsubmit) plus `crud.table.plugin`.
nodes.artefact: nct.tab.plugin + nct.parsis.plugin children
nodes.antiPattern: Modelling case children as document lines (`insert_/delete_<lines>`) when each child needs its own filter, its own row actions and its own export — lines cannot carry any of those.

nodes.name: One form group, two forms, chosen by predicate
nodes.rule: Put a stricter variant of a form in the same form group and let `predicateFormMapping` pick it: `{Extended Case Form <- 'Case Has Exposure', Standard Case Form <- 'True'}` — no second button, no second screen, no branch in a rule.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.formGroups[].predicateFormMapping
nodes.antiPattern: A single mega-form with 12 conditionally hidden origination fields, or a second row action the analyst has to know to press.

nodes.name: Validation rules that refuse, name the field, and speak the user's language
nodes.rule: Attach VALIDATION_RULEs to the FORM's `validators[]`, build a message map keyed by locale, read `service.global.locale.getKey()`, and call `validation.addFieldError("<Field label>", msg)` so the message lands on the offending field; read thresholds from the policy table, not from constants.
nodes.artefact: VALIDATION_RULE in rep-objects.forms[].validators
nodes.antiPattern: `validation.addError("Invalid")` in one language: the officer cannot tell which field is wrong, and the compliance evidence that the refusal happened is unreadable to the auditor.

nodes.name: Documents in the customer's language, selected by alias suffix
nodes.rule: Create one PDF and one mail template per language with the language in the alias (`decisionLetterPdfHy|Ru|En`), branch three ways at the call site on the CUSTOMER's `preferredLanguage`, and treat a null PDF reference as fatal so the record is never marked notified without a document.
nodes.artefact: pdfTemplates + mailTemplates + service.report.pdf.get/email
nodes.antiPattern: Rendering in the operator's interface locale, or swallowing a null reference from `service.report.pdf.get` and still stamping `customerNotifiedAt`.

nodes.name: One export template for every register — scoped, and auditing itself
nodes.rule: Give every table a `direct: true` Export action guarded by one role predicate, render through a single generic `registerExportPdf({title, info, items})`, re-apply the caller's row scope before selecting, and write an `action:'EXPORT'` audit row recording who took how many rows.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE + one pdfTemplate + auditEntry CRUD
nodes.antiPattern: An export that bypasses the find rule's scope (a branch user exports every branch) or that leaves no trace — "who took a copy of the register" is itself a supervisory question.

nodes.name: Business configuration governed like a business document
nodes.rule: Give config tables `approvalState/proposedBy/proposedAt/approvedBy/approvedAt/pendingNote` plus Submit-for-approval → Approve/Reject actions, hook a generic before-save diff rule that writes one audit row per changed field stamped with the current `policyVersion`, and add a re-apply action that re-scores open AND parked work and reports what moved.
nodes.artefact: reference CRUDs + generic EXECUTION_RULE as onBeforeComplete
nodes.antiPattern: The generic diff rule iterating a hard-coded alias array — add a table and it silently audits nothing; and re-scoring only OPEN work, so parked cases keep a priority computed by a version that no longer exists.

nodes.name: Server-filtered relation dropdown with a disambiguating label
nodes.rule: Set `searchEnabled:true` + `searchRuleIdentifier` + `prevRuleIdentifier` on the field and back it with a rule that reads `attrs.filterBy` through a Jackson-safe `_txt()`, caps at 20 rows, and returns a composed `label` (`customerNo — fullName`) with `displayName:"label"` so duplicates are distinguishable.
nodes.artefact: dynaform.form.rimm.drop.down.field.plugin settings + choices rule
nodes.antiPattern: `toString()` on a Jackson TextNode (keeps the quotes) or `as int` on an IntNode (throws); and `displayName:"fullName"` when four rows share a name — the picker shows four identical options.

nodes.name: One shared left nav, grouped by job, gated per role group
nodes.rule: Write quick links only into the shared `virtualPlugins[] "Nct left nav"` node, group entries by the way a job is done (Cases · Restrictions · Regulator · Oversight · Configuration · Reports · admin), give each entry a `pe-7s-*` icon, and set `roleAccess.roleGroupAccessors` from the PRD's own access matrix so a role sees only its own work.
nodes.artefact: site.kicker.plugin modelGroups on the shared virtual plugin
nodes.antiPattern: Editing the per-page kicker nodes (dead data — never read at runtime), and leaving role-group names inherited from a template project: one entry here is gated to five role groups that do not exist, so the home dashboard is invisible in the menu to every real role.

nodes.name: Every rule carries its requirement ids and its library reference
nodes.rule: Put the PRD ids in the rule `description` ("FR-22 / BR-05 / A-04 — the aggregate at a party is the SUM across every path") and the governing library section in an inline comment ("SHAPE C: the SYSTEM opens the case (doc 27 §4-§5)", "doc 15 §6: a null reference means no document exists").
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.rules[].description + Groovy comments
nodes.antiPattern: A rule named "Update Case 2" with an empty description — six months later nobody can tell whether it is load-bearing or a leftover, and no coverage gate can prove the requirement was built.

nodes.name: Soft delete with partial unique indexes and CHECK-constrained enums
nodes.rule: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_<t>_<col> ON …(<col>) WHERE (deleted = false)` on every business key (28 of them here), a `CHECK (col = ANY (ARRAY[...]))` per enum column mirrored by an `ENUM_*` choices rule, and `ON CONFLICT … WHERE deleted = false DO UPDATE` upserts riding the same index.
nodes.artefact: project-db.dump schema + dynamic-CRUD SQL methods
nodes.antiPattern: A plain UNIQUE on a soft-deleted table — deleting and re-creating the same code then fails; and an ON CONFLICT whose target index does not exist, which fails only at the first collision.

nodes.name: Frontier aggregation over a chain of movements
nodes.rule: When money (or goods, or custody) moves in a chain, the total at a party is the SUM over every branch keyed by party+institution, and what is still recoverable is only the hops with no onward child and no terminal flag — summing every non-terminal hop counts the same value once per link.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE behind a direct row action
nodes.antiPattern: Taking the largest branch as the exposure (understates split transfers), or summing all non-terminal hops (double counts the chain). Also: a loop must be flagged and the calculation must still complete, not abort.

nodes.name: Scheduler = predicate gate + action rule + service user
nodes.rule: Pair every `RUN_RULE` scheduler with a PREDICATE (`There Are Overdue Items To Chase`, `It Is The First Of The Month`) so the action never runs on an empty set, run it as a named service account, and bound the sweep (`passes`, `rowsInPage`, break when a pass claims nothing) so a backlog drains over ticks.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.schedulers[] (job.expression + predicateIdentifier + actionRuleIdentifier)
nodes.antiPattern: An unbounded `while(true)` sweep that times out on a first-run backlog, and shipping every scheduler `enabled: false` with nothing in the handoff telling the operator to switch them on.

nodes.name: The status machine as a row of gated buttons
nodes.rule: Every crud.table editAction = an `X Is <Status>` PREDICATE + an `onBeforeCompleteRuleIdentifier` that performs exactly that transition; `direct:true` for one-click, a formGroup when input is needed — and the rule re-checks the status server-side because a hidden button is not a guarantee.
nodes.artefact: crud.table.plugin model.editActions[] + PREDICATE rules named `<Entity> Is <Status>` + EXECUTION_RULE per transition
nodes.antiPattern: A generic Edit form with a free status dropdown; or a predicate that gates the button but no `if (row.status != 'X') throw` inside the rule.

nodes.name: One named SQL method per state transition
nodes.rule: Never `update(status:…)` — each transition is its own CRUD method (`approve`, `postpone`, `escalate`, `reopen`, `send`, `confirm`, `dispatch`, `clearHold`, `markReceived`, `post`, `submit`, `close`) that also stamps its own timestamp/actor columns and clamps its own inputs in SQL.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json methods[] of type SQL, one per verb
nodes.antiPattern: `postpone` implemented as a generic update — the clamp `LEAST(GREATEST(:days,1),14)` and `postpone_count = postpone_count + 1` then live in Groovy and drift from the UI.

nodes.name: The header+lines quintet, and json_agg for the grid
nodes.rule: A document CRUD is recognisable by exactly five methods — `createHeader / insertLine / deleteLines / _deleteHeader / findLines` — with `create`/`delete` as thin Groovy wrappers, `recomputeTotals` as one `UPDATE h … FROM (SELECT … GROUP BY)`, and `findAll` carrying the lines inline as a correlated `json_agg(...)` COALESCEd to `'[]'::json`.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json method set + dynaform.form.list.field.plugin bound to `fieldExpression:"lines"` with `__temp_list_item_context__` / `__temp_item__` sub-form controls
nodes.antiPattern: Omitting the COALESCE so a header with no lines answers `null` — the list control renders nothing and the first line can never be added.

nodes.name: A threshold rule shipped as an editable band table
nodes.rule: Any PRD sentence of the form "if X ≤ a then A, else if X ≤ b then B…" becomes a register (code, value, `max_<x>` ceiling, sort_order, active, description) + one `selectFor<X>` SQL — `WHERE active AND (ceiling IS NULL OR :x <= ceiling) ORDER BY value ASC LIMIT 1` — + a page, with the PRD clause text stored in each row's `description`.
nodes.artefact: a dynamic CRUD + one SQL method + one crud.table page; the rule that uses it only publishes the answer into context attrs
nodes.antiPattern: The if/else ladder written in Groovy — then every threshold change is a rebuild, and nobody can see why 26 is 26.

nodes.name: Versioned parameters, and the snapshot that makes them useful
nodes.rule: Parameters get their own register with `version` / `effective_from` / `status DRAFT→ACTIVE→SUPERSEDED` and three methods (`nextVersion`, `activate` which computes every derived quantity in SQL, `supersedeOthers`); the other half is that each document LINE stores the parameters it was computed from — one `<param>_at_calc` column per parameter, plus the derived daily rate.
nodes.artefact: itemParameter CRUD (12 methods) + partial unique index on (item_id, version) + `Create Item Parameter Version` rule copying the ACTIVE one to a new DRAFT
nodes.antiPattern: Editing the ACTIVE version in place — every report computed before the edit becomes unexplainable; and versioning the register without snapshotting onto the document, which is only half the job.

nodes.name: One home for every derived number
nodes.rule: Derived quantities are computed only by named SQL CRUD methods (`recalculate`, `activate`, `recomputeTotals`, `allocateLandedCost`) so the grid, the row action and the nightly job cannot disagree; the Groovy rule around each one is three lines of orchestration.
nodes.artefact: SQL CRUD methods; EXECUTION_RULEs that only call them
nodes.antiPattern: Recomputing IP in Groovy in the job and again in a rule — plus the Postgres trap: inside one UPDATE every RHS column reference is the PRE-update value, so a derived column must repeat the whole expression, not read the column being written.

nodes.name: Opening a case by itself, idempotently
nodes.rule: Three columns on the subject row (`process_started_at`, `process_identifier`, `process_start_count`) + gather → claim → shape → start → mark, where the claim is one conditional `UPDATE … WHERE status='NEW' AND process_started_at IS NULL RETURNING *` (null = somebody else won), a repair sweep runs FIRST and hands back claims older than 5 min with no process id, and `endCase` clears both when a branch closes the case so a later cycle can open a fresh one.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE + PREDICATE gate + scheduler `RUN_RULE`; 7 SQL methods on the subject CRUD; `service.workflow.start(id, {contextDataMap, attrs}, {roleGroups, businessKey, groupIdentifier})`
nodes.antiPattern: start-then-mark (a crash leaves a case whose row was never marked, the next tick opens a duplicate and no screen can tell them apart); omitting `groupIdentifier` (the worklist's inner join hides the case and nothing is logged) or `roleGroups` (only admins and authors can see it, and testing as the author proves nothing); forgetting `endCase`, so a postponed-then-reopened row stays claimed for ever.

nodes.name: A workflow screen can only render GLOBAL attributes
nodes.rule: Neither a user-task form nor a process-table column is ever bound to a CRUD row, so the first service task copies the subject's human-readable fields into GLOBAL attrs (`case*`), every later service task republishes what it just made true, and even a row action ends with `context.data.setAttr('caseStatus', …)` because a published attribute is a COPY, not a view.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE wired as the first service task; dynaform form with `scope:"GLOBAL"` + `alwaysProhibited:true` controls; process.table.pluin columnSettings with `scope:"GLOBAL"`
nodes.antiPattern: Publishing an attribute once at the start and never again — the worklist then shows a frozen copy that drifts from every other screen. And there is no way to render a child grid this way: lines arrive as a newline-joined string in a textarea.

nodes.name: The side-form that silently does nothing
nodes.rule: A small input form for a row action (postpone days, a tracking reference, an added cost, adjustment quantities) written with `scope:"GLOBAL"` controls and read by the rule with `context.data.getAttr(...)` works from a workflow task and SILENTLY NO-OPS from a CRUD-table row action, because the runtime rebinds every control to the table's crud alias: the attr is null, the method receives '', COALESCE keeps the old value, and the action reports success.
nodes.artefact: dynaform.form.*.field.plugin `settings.scope` + the EXECUTION_RULE that reads them
nodes.antiPattern: This IS the anti-pattern. Fix: declare the controls `scope:"CRUD"` with the table's contextIdentifier + crudAlias; for a form opened from BOTH a row action and a task, read attrs first and fall back to `context.<ctx>.<alias>.data.get()`.

nodes.name: Row scoping belongs in the fetch rule
nodes.rule: "An action predicate hides a button, it never removes a row from a list" — the same CRUD becomes two workplaces by giving each page its own `Find`/`Fetch` rule that forwards the filter bar's attrs and THEN overwrites the scope key (so a crafted filter cannot widen it), with a fail-closed sentinel like '__none__'.
nodes.artefact: crud.table.plugin `findRuleIdentifier` → EXECUTION_RULE forwarding `attrs` (skipping keys starting with `_`)
nodes.antiPattern: Writing the scope before the forwarding loop, so a hand-crafted filter parameter overwrites it; or relying on the action predicate to keep other people's rows off the screen.

nodes.name: Every scheduled job writes its own audit row
nodes.rule: The job opens a run record, does its work, then `finish(items_checked, items_affected, items_created, status, message)` with a human sentence; one crud.table page over that register IS the operator's proof the job ran, and it carries the manual `direct:true` "Run it now" button that calls the very same rule.
nodes.artefact: a register CRUD with `create` + `finish`; scheduler `actionType: RUN_RULE`; a createAction with `direct:true` and a role predicate
nodes.antiPattern: A silent scheduler. Also: an optional sub-step that may be undeployed after import must be try/caught and recorded in the run message, not allowed to fail the whole job.

nodes.name: Anchor the rolling window on MAX(data), not on now()
nodes.rule: Every trend query reads `>= date_trunc('month',(SELECT MAX(ts) FROM …)) - INTERVAL '12 months'` and `< date_trunc('month',(SELECT MAX(ts) …))`, and the period-lookup that feeds the "Since" filter is built from the same expression — so a restored dump, a demo or a UAT environment always renders a full year and the filter can never offer an empty period.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects queries[] behind chart.js `$$()` replacements
nodes.antiPattern: `WHERE ts >= now() - INTERVAL '12 months'` — every chart on a restored PoC is empty and the demo dies.

nodes.name: Nav: the author's drawer and the user's drawer
nodes.rule: Exactly two groups in the shared `Nct left nav` — the baseline `Pages` console left untouched, and one business-named group holding Home (moved OUT of Pages) plus the business pages ordered the way work flows: dashboards, then live work in chain order, then registers, then configuration; form-group and form pages are children, never nav entries.
nodes.artefact: branch.virtualPlugins[] name="Nct left nav" → content.properties.modelGroups
nodes.antiPattern: This project's own defect: the trilingual labels were written on the inner `linkModel.localizedMap` instead of the nav ITEM's `localizedMap.name`, so the whole sidebar renders in one language under every locale (13 validate errors).

nodes.name: The `_rid` helper — one rule for a button and a service task
nodes.rule: A four-line closure resolves "which row am I acting on" from three surfaces in order (`context.<ctx>.<alias>.data.get()`, `attrs._crudEntityId`, `context.data.getAttr(alias+'Id')`) and republishes the id, which is what lets the SAME execution rule back a table row action and a BPMN service task; it travels with `CALL` (unwraps nested causes and names the failing rule), `NUM` (always BigDecimal, never BigInteger) and `_c` (normalise a paged find).
nodes.artefact: copy-pasted Groovy closures at the top of ~40 EXECUTION_RULEs
nodes.antiPattern: Writing the transition twice, once for the button and once for the task — they diverge on the first change. Also `0G` instead of `0.0G`: a BigInteger literal that only surfaces on inputs the PRD's own example never produces.

nodes.name: Idempotency by counting the journal, not by a flag
nodes.rule: A step that can fire from two surfaces guards itself with `countByReference(reference_id, movement_type) > 0` against the append-only movement journal it is about to write — the audit trail doubles as the idempotency key, with no `processed` boolean to keep in sync.
nodes.artefact: an append-only journal table (no modification_time, no update path, no row actions) + a `countByReference` SQL method
nodes.antiPattern: A `processed` flag on the document, which can be true while the journal rows were rolled back.

nodes.name: One help bubble per form, explaining the rule
nodes.rule: Each form carries at least one `nct.help.plugin` with `alwaysVisible:true`, `showMessageOn:"CLICK"` and a `localizedMap.message` in every tenant locale that states the BUSINESS RULE behind the field — "Between 1 and 14 days (UI-1); the warning reopens automatically" — often citing the requirement clause by number.
nodes.artefact: nct.help.plugin node beside the label inside the generated `gen_slot_*` html
nodes.antiPattern: Help text that restates the label ("Enter the postpone days") instead of the rule the user cannot see.

nodes.name: Gate the `Pages` drawer on the group node; never reorder or rewrite it
nodes.rule: Leave `Pages` at order 0 with its baseline uuid `62492f05-4e61-42dd-a659-6a391504e843`, delete only its `Home` child (leaving an order-0 hole and children at 1..14), and put one `roleAccess` on the GROUP granting `Author` (+ admin/nct_author via `accessors`) with `publicReadAccess:false` — the group prunes, so the 14 console links need no edits at all.
nodes.artefact: branch.virtualPlugins[name=='Nct left nav'].content.properties.modelGroups.stringValue → pagesModel[0]
nodes.antiPattern: A left `Home` inside `Pages`, added the whole business app as a second order-0 sibling there, and set `publicReadAccess:true` on the group so every end user sees Rules/Contexts/Database/Business Logic/Schedulers. Doc 17 instead tells you to put business groups FIRST — three of three projects ignored that and gated instead, which is idempotent under re-running `quicklink add --group Pages` and does not renumber the baseline.

nodes.name: Cross-check every `roleGroupAccessors` key against the project's real role groups
nodes.rule: Three of four exports gate nav items to five role groups that exist in none of them — `Software Specialist`, `Front Office Employee`, `Diagnostic Technician`, `Diagnostic Head`, `Hardware Specialist` — inherited from a template and never rewritten; with `accessors: {}` alongside, the item is visible to nobody but `Author`.

nodes.name: The Labels + Ids + Values three-column contract
nodes.rule: Every category chart binds three replacements from one query — a human display label, the raw DB code, and the measure — so the axis reads, the colour map keys on a stable value, and crossFilter sends something WHERE can match.

nodes.name: cssByTheme as a per-theme palette bridge
nodes.rule: Declare 19 colour tokens (--c1..--c8 qualitative, --c-good/warn/risk/crit/mute, --r1..--r4 sequential, --div-up/down) on the mount class in cssByTheme with a light '*' block and a lightened block per dark skin, then read them back in JS with getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue — the canvas gets a palette that re-tints per theme.
nodes.artefact: ChartJsModel.cssByTheme + a V(name,fallback) helper at the top of every chart's js
nodes.antiPattern: Pasting raw hex literals into every chart's js (C, 14 hexes × 87 charts): correct on the light skin, a hole on the four dark ones, and unfixable without editing 87 nodes.

nodes.name: Every visible string is a sibling nct.label.plugin, never chart text
nodes.rule: The chart node carries no words at all; board title, section heading, chart title and chart subtitle are label nodes (tagName h6/span) whose localizedStringValue holds en_US/ru_RU/hy_AM — because js, html and cssByTheme are one non-localized string each.
nodes.artefact: nct.label.plugin siblings inside the grid nct.html.plugin; only 2 of the 185 charts use plugins.title, neither on a board
nodes.antiPattern: D typed the chart's title into the chart's own html in 12 of 12 charts while its section headings were trilingual labels — the board shows headings in one locale above chart titles in another the moment the user switches language. Doc 22 §2B.5's own 'title inside the chart, align:start' bullet causes this.

nodes.name: query.parameters ships the author's last preview pick
nodes.rule: The editor persists whatever filter value you previewed with into the embedded query's parameters map, so the board opens pre-filtered and a customer's supplier/category name is baked into the shipped JSON.
nodes.artefact: replacements[].query.parameters — must be {} or {"value": null} before pack
nodes.antiPattern: Shipping {"Supplier":{"value":"<a customer's supplier>"}} — every KPI and bar on the board opens filtered to one entity and the reviewer's first impression is numbers that do not match the data.

nodes.name: The selector must not declare its own dimension — audited, not assumed
nodes.rule:
A chart that GROUP BYs a column and also declares {name:'

'} on it collapses to a single mark on the first click; the check is mechanical (does the crossFilter param appear as a placeholder in the same SQL text) and must be run, because eyes miss it.
nodes.artefact: the chart's embedded SQL vs its js crossFilter call; audit script in §11 check 2

nodes.name: The period filter is named Since and compared with >=
nodes.rule: 284 placeholder occurrences across three projects, zero equalities: AND to_char(<date>,'YYYY-MM') >= {name:'Since', type:'dropdown-string', dropDownPopulation:{…}}, with the lookup UNIONing every fact table's date on a multi-fact board.
