nodes.antiPattern: An `=` period (most cells of the filter cross-product return nothing) or a scalar `date` param (never substitutes at all).

nodes.name: Every chart's js opens with a theme prelude
nodes.rule: 185/185 charts read live colours off the mounted element before constructing anything: Chart.defaults.color = getComputedStyle(host).color, Chart.defaults.borderColor from --bs-border-color, plus Intl.NumberFormat formatters and a shared base(legend) options factory.
nodes.artefact: the first ~20 lines of ChartJsModel.js, pasted identically into every chart of a board
nodes.antiPattern: Letting Chart.js keep its hardcoded #666 text and rgba(0,0,0,0.1) gridlines — 2.2:1 on the four dark skins, invisible gridlines.

nodes.name: Plotly indicator tiles: number, number+delta, gauge+bands
nodes.rule: Three verified skeletons on transparent paper — a plain number (92–118px), a period-over-period delta whose Value and Prev come from one FILTER-ed aggregate, and a gauge whose bar colour, number colour and band are all driven by the value.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin with a <div> mount (no canvas), Plotly.newPlot + paper_bgcolor/plot_bgcolor rgba(0,0,0,0) + ResizeObserver
nodes.antiPattern: Omitting ResizeObserver (17 of 49 tiles do — they never resize when their Bootstrap column does), forgetting gauge.bgcolor (Plotly paints the gauge white even with paper_bgcolor transparent), and leaving increasing/decreasing at default polarity on a loss metric.

nodes.name: Two series from one query — SQL FILTER pivot vs JS pivot()
nodes.rule: Fixed, known series (on-time/late, critical/high) pivot in SQL with count(*) FILTER (WHERE …) and bind one $$() per series; data-driven series pivot in JS from a long (key, series, value) triple with an explicit ORDER array so the stack never reshuffles.
nodes.artefact: chart SQL + the pivot()/mapof() helpers in ChartJsModel.js
nodes.antiPattern: A JS pivot whose series order comes from the data (segments reshuffle between renders) instead of from a declared ORDER array with a fallback slot.

nodes.name: One nct.html.plugin per band, semantic slot identifiers, nct.parsis cells
nodes.rule: Split the board into header / filter bar / filter hint / KPI band / one node per section row, name each slot identifier readably (h-r1c2, rop-kpi-3, <row>-hdr), and hang each chart inside an nct.parsis.plugin cell rather than in the grid slot directly.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin.html with <plugin id="…" name="nct.parsis.plugin"> slots matching each child's `identifier` (not id, not uniqueIdentifier, not name)
nodes.antiPattern: One 6 KB html one-liner holding all five cards with uuid4 slot identifiers — every row edit re-emits the whole page and nobody can read the tree.

nodes.name: Full arrives as a string or as column-metadata rows — normalise before reading
nodes.rule: A `Full` replacement can land as JSON text (so rows.length counts characters and rows[0] is '['), and each row is {cols:[{column:{name},<value>}]} not a plain map; asRows()+flattenRow() handle every observed shape and a COLS literal lets a positional row still be read by name.
nodes.artefact: ChartJsModel.js helper pair, used with a <div> mount and C.find('.x').html(...) — the data-bound HTML tile
nodes.antiPattern: rows[0] / rows.length straight off $$('rows',[],'Full') — the tile prints 0 with correct SQL and no error, which cost three rounds of fixes to diagnose.

nodes.name: Resolving the session locale inside the chart's own JS
nodes.rule: ?lng= → ?lang= → `lang` cookie → <html lang> gives the chart the locale the user is reading, and L(en,hy) / W(dbValue) then localize the strings that must live inside the plot — dataset labels, axis units, tooltip prefixes, empty states.
nodes.artefact: an IIFE at the top of ChartJsModel.js, plus a WORDS dictionary for enum values that arrive in one language
nodes.antiPattern: One-way swapping (replace English, keep no copy) — switching back leaves every static label stranded in the other language; and treating a default 'en_US' as evidence of English when <html lang> says otherwise.

nodes.name: Bar colour computed per row from sibling threshold series
nodes.rule: Bind the measure plus its two limits from the same query and colour each bar by comparing them (x <= reorder ? red : x <= warning ? amber : green), then draw the two limits as reference lines — one chart that says both 'how much' and 'is it a problem'.
nodes.artefact: 3 extra Double[] replacements + a backgroundColor map function in ChartJsModel.js
nodes.antiPattern: A flat magnitude bar plus a separate 'breaches' chart — two cells to answer one question, and the reader has to join them by eye.

nodes.name: State the scope in the title or subtitle when a chart cannot take a page filter
nodes.rule: A chart whose source has no date column simply ends its name in '— now' or '— last 12 months', or says it in its localizable subtitle label; both cost nothing and stop the board silently contradicting itself.
nodes.artefact: the chart node's name, or the <cell>-s subtitle nct.label.plugin
nodes.antiPattern: Leaving it silent — the unfiltered chart keeps showing whole-dataset numbers next to filtered neighbours and nothing reports it.

nodes.name: One aggregate query, N KPI tiles, maxItemsCount 1
nodes.rule: When several tiles share a WHERE, write one query returning several aggregate columns and give each tile the same embedded query with a different columnName and maxItemsCount:1; split only when the tiles genuinely need different windows.
nodes.artefact: identical replacements[].query across nodes, differing columnName + maxItemsCount
nodes.antiPattern: One query per tile out of habit — four plans to tune and four places a definition can drift apart.

nodes.name: Two-tier token block: chrome from platform tokens, status ramp your own
nodes.rule: In `css.byTheme["*"]` a `:root` block binds surface/text/border two-level (`var(--current-line, #fff)`) but declares accent and ok/warn/bad/info as your OWN light literals, then four byte-identical dark-skin blocks redeclare only those 6-8 semantic tokens with measured >=4.5:1 values — 755 B per dark key, byte-identical across all four in 22/22 components (~150 B of it declarations), against a 22 KB shared block, and the primary button's foreground inverts (dark label on a light mint fill) because white-on-accent cannot reach 4.5:1 on a dark skin.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin -> properties.studioModel -> css.byTheme ("*" + "Dark"/"Dracula"/"Forest"/"Dark Blue"); chart.js.plugin -> properties.Javascript -> cssByTheme
nodes.antiPattern: Binding status colours to `var(--green, var(--bs-success))` per 24a §3.2: on Dracula --green is a blue and --cyan==--pink==--purple, on Dark Blue --green==--purple, so the whole ok/info/accent ramp collapses to one hue and measures 2-3:1 on the card surface.

nodes.name: The zero-CSS console vocabulary
nodes.rule: A console is `main-card mb-3 card` panels, each with a `card-header` carrying one `lnr-*` icon in the project's SINGLE `icon-gradient bg-*` class plus an `nct.label.plugin` title, a `row g-4` of `col-12 col-lg-*` cells, and an empty `nct.parsis.plugin` in every cell — structure in the html node, content swappable without touching layout.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin (no studioModel) hosting <plugin> tags; nct.parsis.plugin slots; nct.label.plugin strings
nodes.antiPattern: Typing visible strings into markup (kills localization) and placing plugins as siblings in one slot instead of nesting slots inside your own structure; `bg-plum-plate` varied per section, which turns headers into decoration instead of a system (39 of 39 real occurrences use the same gradient).

nodes.name: One slot, four sentences — the whole loading/empty/error/crash vocabulary
nodes.rule: The primary content region ships `Loading…` as AUTHORED markup so the first paint is never blank, and the same cell later carries the empty sentence (specific: "No invoices match these filters.", never "No data"), the error sentence (`Could not load <the thing>: ` + server message) and — from a try/catch wrapping the entire script — `Script error: …`; no spinner, no skeleton, no overlay.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code + the `<pfx>-empty` class in css.byTheme["*"]
nodes.antiPattern: A blank slot on first paint, and a generic "No data" that cannot distinguish "nothing matched your filter" from "the load failed".

nodes.name: Promote page actions into the breadcrumb by proxying the existing DOM button
nodes.rule: A shared JS_CLASSIC lib mirrors a screen's own `<button>` into a `ctx.breadcrumb` descriptor and forwards the click — `el.style.display='none'` (hidden, not removed, so the screen still reads/writes disabled and textContent), a MutationObserver on `['disabled','hidden','title']` republishes labels and enabled state, ancestor `[hidden]` removes grouped actions, and the spinner resolves on the FIRST disabled-mutation after the click (never by re-reading the final state, which hangs when a screen disables→enables→disables in one synchronous block).
nodes.artefact: studioModel.libs[] -> {kind:JS_CLASSIC, path:"studio/<kit>/<kit>.js", globalVar:"…"} + ctx.breadcrumb.set()
nodes.antiPattern: A hand-built toolbar inside the component — the single most reliable tell that a console was hand-built, because it will never match the theme's buttons on all five skins.

nodes.name: One kit prefix per PROJECT, shipped as a CSS lib asset — not one kit per component
nodes.rule: Split authored CSS three ways: the shared kit (layout/type/spacing, colour only via `--<pfx>-*`) as a `kind:"CSS"` lib asset in tenant-files, one copy; the token block plus this screen's unique classes in `css.byTheme["*"]`; the semantic ramp in the four dark keys — accepting that a CSS lib asset is page-global and unscoped, so every selector must carry the prefix and no bare `.card`/`table`/`h1` selector may exist.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.libs[].assets[] {kind:"CSS", path:"studio/<pfx>-kit/<pfx>-kit.css"} + css.byTheme
nodes.antiPattern: Renaming the starter kit's prefix per component: a class defined in one component does not exist in another, so `app-chip` written into a second screen renders unstyled even though markup and data are correct.

nodes.name: The KPI tile that is also a filter
nodes.rule: An interactive KPI is a real `<button>` un-styled in four declarations (`appearance:none;text-align:left;font:inherit;width:100%`) with `aria-pressed`, and its selected state is a border + 2px ring — never a fill, so the number stays the brightest thing; an inert tile stays a `<div>`, so the affordance is structural and cannot drift.
nodes.artefact: main html document + css.byTheme["*"]
nodes.antiPattern: A clickable `<div class="kpi">` with a JS click handler — no keyboard, no focus ring, no announced state; and a filled selected state that outshouts the value it is supposed to be showing.

nodes.name: Mid-grey at low alpha as the token-free theme-safe fill
nodes.rule: `rgba(127,127,127,.10–.28)` lightens a dark surface and darkens a light one by roughly the same perceptual amount, so one literal is correct on all five skins with no token, no fallback and no color-mix — and it is the only option inside a JS string, where CSS variables are unreachable.
nodes.artefact: css.byTheme["*"] and chart.js.plugin -> model.js
nodes.antiPattern: `rgba(255,255,255,.03)` or `rgba(0,0,0,.05)` — invisible on one half of the skin matrix; and `rgba(var(--bs-primary-rgb), .12)`, whose -rgb companion is Standard-only so the whole declaration is dropped on all four dark skins.

nodes.name: Four named chart ramps declared in cssByTheme, read in js with getComputedStyle
nodes.rule: The container class declares categorical `--c1…c8`, semantic `--c-good/warn/risk/crit/mute`, sequential `--r1…r4` and diverging `--div-up/--div-down` in `cssByTheme["*"]` (light) and again, lifted and desaturated, in the four dark keys; the js reads them with a `V(name, fallback)` helper off `getComputedStyle(container)` and sets `paper_bgcolor/plot_bgcolor:'rgba(0,0,0,0)'` and `font.color: cs.color` live — so a new skin needs no js edit.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin -> properties.Javascript -> {cssByTheme, html, js}
nodes.antiPattern: A palette hard-coded in the chart's `js`, or a `<style>` block inside the chart's `html` — the latter is page-global and one audited delivery had fifteen sibling panels depending on a single panel's style block.

nodes.name: The measured px scale a bespoke console actually needs
nodes.rule: Type 28-31/22-23/15-16.5/13-13.5/12/11-11.5/10 px at weights 600 and 700 only, uppercase 11px labels at .05–.06em; radius in three tiers (999px pill / 12px panel / 8px control, plus 4px icon and 50% avatar); gaps and padding on a 4px grid; alpha .12–.16 fill, .35 border, .08–.10 row state; ONE `@media (max-width:900px)` breakpoint (21 of 22 components) collapsing the deliberate two-column split, everything else `repeat(auto-fit,minmax(190px,1fr))`; seven transitions in 540 KB of CSS, all .12s.
nodes.artefact: css.byTheme["*"]
nodes.antiPattern: A breakpoint per component and hand-tuned column counts; and `rem` in a component whose root font size it does not control.

nodes.name: The `<pfx>-msg` strip: classList, empty-hides, clear-before/re-assert-after, one busy flag
nodes.rule: `display:none` by default with `.show` + `.ok`/`.err`; manipulate with `classList` never `className` (which deletes the class the element was found by, so the next query returns null and every later message is swallowed); an empty message HIDES the strip; the action clears it before the call and re-asserts it after the reload; one module-level `busy` flag disables the button and answers a click-while-busy with a sentence, not silence.
nodes.artefact: css.byTheme["*"] (.\<pfx\>-msg) + studioModel.scripts[].code
nodes.antiPattern: `el.className = 'app-msg show ok'`; a success-styled empty box after an HTTP 200; a stale message that outlives the action that wrote it. Also: the strip carries no `aria-live` in any of these projects — add `aria-live="polite"`.

nodes.name: `opacity` instead of a muted-colour token
nodes.rule: For de-emphasised text inside an authored component, `opacity:.7–.8` inherits the skin's own text colour, cannot go out of contrast range, cannot pick a Standard-only token and needs no fallback — reach for `var(--comment, …)` only when you need a different HUE, not a different weight.
nodes.artefact: cssByTheme["*"] / css.byTheme["*"]
nodes.antiPattern: A grey literal (`#6b7280`) for captions, and a bare `var(--comment)` with no fallback, which is silently dropped on Standard.

nodes.name: The paper exception — the one place #fff/#000 is correct
nodes.rule: A document-preview sheet is `background:#ffffff;color:#000000;width:210mm;max-width:100%;padding:10mm` with `:empty{display:none}` so it is never a blank white slab, and `@media print` hides the app chrome, forces `print-color-adjust:exact` on zebra fills, sets `page-break-inside:avoid` on every row-bearing element and `@page{size:A4 portrait;margin:10mm}`.
nodes.artefact: css.byTheme["*"] including an @media print block
nodes.antiPattern: Tokenising a document preview so it turns dark on a dark skin — the user is previewing what the printer will produce.

nodes.name: Icon font for platform markup, inline SVG with currentColor inside a component
nodes.rule: `lnr-*` in card headers and `pe-7s-*` in breadcrumb buttons inherit `color` and match every stock plugin; inside a studio component use inline SVG at 15-16px with `stroke="currentColor" fill="none" stroke-width="2"` round caps and `aria-hidden="true"`, because the font classes are page-global and unscoped while an SVG that carries no colour of its own is theme-safe by construction.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin html property; ctx.breadcrumb descriptor `icon` field
nodes.antiPattern: An SVG with a hard `fill="#…"`, and a `<span class="badge">` or `badge-light` used as a status chip — both are 0 occurrences here, correctly.

nodes.name: Gate every var() — an undefined alias silently un-styles the control
nodes.rule: An undefined custom property with no fallback invalidates the WHOLE declaration at computed-value time, so a five-token typo renders a panel completely unstyled with no console error and no validate warning; a ~25-line walk over studioModel.css.byTheme and chart cssByTheme that reports any `var(--x)` which is neither defined locally nor one of the 24a §3.1 platform tokens closes it.
nodes.artefact: a pre-pack script over branches.json (studioModel.css.byTheme + chart cssByTheme/css)
nodes.antiPattern: Trusting `validate` — its literal-hex check never resolves a var(), never parses a selector, and never reads a chart's CSS.

nodes.name: Three interaction rules that keep a console honest
nodes.rule: (1) A control that discloses must say what it opened, bring it into view, and never share a caption with the control that acts — an edit form must never look like a create form. (2) Before disabling a control, find the rule that already refuses; the greyed control states the conclusion and withholds the reason, and it drifts. (3) A field that cannot be computed says why in the space it occupies — removing it is not a message, and a KPI with no data shows an em dash, never 0.
nodes.artefact: main html document + the `<pfx>-note` class in css.byTheme["*"]
nodes.antiPattern: Hiding an inapplicable field (a vanishing field teaches nothing), a disabled control standing in for a server rule, and a zero rendered in 28px bold where the query returned nothing.

nodes.name: The accessors stanza is boilerplate, and it silently bypasses persona gating
nodes.rule: Only 7 distinct `accessors` maps exist across 18,636 nodes; the default on business pages ("stanza B") sets view:true on user_*, role_group_* and file_storage_*, and the page check is `public OR authenticated OR anyAccessor OR anyRoleGroupAccessor` — so any persona holding one of those platform roles opens the page whatever roleGroupAccessors says.
nodes.artefact: branches.json → siteMapPage.roleAccess.accessors (27 fixed keys) vs rep-objects.roleGroups[].roles[]
nodes.antiPattern: Ticking roleGroupAccessors and assuming the page is now persona-only, while leaving the default 12-view-true accessors stanza and a persona holding FILE_STORAGE_VIEW.

nodes.name: Hand-write roleGroups[].roles — start from REPORT_VIEW only
nodes.rule: Two projects shipped the Role Management "select all" default — a byte-identical 21-role blob (_REPORT_ROLES minus ADMIN/NCT_AUTHOR/USER_*/ROLE_GROUP_*) on every persona; the two that hand-tuned gave a nine-persona system nothing but REPORT_VIEW/REPORT_VIEW_ANY (+REPORT_EDIT) and it works.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json roleGroups[].roles[] · `mrjun.py rolegroup add --role REPORT_VIEW`
nodes.antiPattern: A "Worker" persona holding SOURCE_EDIT, SCHEDULER_EDIT, STORE_EXECUTE_ANY and OYO_PROJECT_CONFIGURATION — and, fatally, FILE_STORAGE_VIEW.

nodes.name: The canonical row-scoping fetch rule: scope written LAST, identity looked up server-side, fail-closed on a non-matching sentinel
nodes.rule: `filter` is built from attrs, then `if (!hasAnyRoleGroup(<oversight…>)) { filter['scopeCol'] = _myScope() }` as the last statement; `_myScope()` reads the caller's scope from a DB table keyed by `service.security.user().email` and returns '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000' (uuid) or '__none__' (text) when it cannot — because the generated SQL treats an empty string as "no filter" and would return everything.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.rules[] GroovyExecutionRule wired via crud.table.plugin properties.model.findRuleIdentifier
nodes.antiPattern: Returning '' on the fail path (the SQL idiom `COALESCE(CAST(NULLIF(CAST(:p AS text),'') …), col)` reads '' as unfiltered → the whole table); or writing the scope before the `attrs?.each` forwarding loop, where a crafted request overwrites it.

nodes.name: Scope the dropdown, the export and the exception list too — not just the table
nodes.rule: The same branch guard appears on four surfaces: the table fetch rule, the RIMM_* choices rule (still ending in toSelectOptions), the Export rule (which also writes an EXPORT audit row with the row count), and purpose-built list methods that take the scope as a declared SQL parameter; child tables with no scope column get it by subquery on the parent.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.rules[] (fetch / choices / export) + dynamic-cruds.json methods[].script
nodes.antiPattern: A scoped case list beside an unscoped case picker: the dropdown offers every branch's cases, one row at a time.

nodes.name: Action predicate template: role check first, re-read the row from the DB, state last
nodes.rule: `if (!hasAnyRoleGroup(…)) { return false }` then resolve the row id from `context.data.getAttr('<entity>Id')` → `'subjectId'` → `service.crud.<alias>.get(id)` → context copy, every read in try/catch(Throwable) defaulting to false, terminating in `['A','B'].contains(state)`.
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.rules[] executor GroovyPredicate, referenced by crud.table model.editActions/createActions/globalActions[].predicateIdentifier
nodes.antiPattern: Reading the row only from `context.<ctx>.<alias>.data.get()` — stale at form-submit re-check and absent outside a seeded context, so the button silently disappears or the gate passes on old state.

nodes.name: Scope by exclusion of the wide roles, never by inclusion of the narrow one
nodes.rule: `if (!hasAnyRoleGroup(<the roles that see everything>)) { scope }` puts every unmapped account, new persona and failed group lookup into the scoped branch; the inverse `if (hasAnyRoleGroup("Supplier") && !hasAnyRoleGroup("Manager") …)` leaves a user with no role at all completely unscoped.
nodes.artefact: the `if` around the scope assignment in any GroovyExecutionRule fetch rule
nodes.antiPattern: Enumerating the restricted persona instead of the privileged ones — adding a seventh persona then silently grants it the whole table.

nodes.name: Separation of duties: compare lowercased e-mails, refuse an empty caller, keep state out of the shared rule
nodes.rule: Role guard, then `def me = (service.security.user()?.email ?: '').toLowerCase(); if (me.isEmpty()) return false`, then refuse when me equals any actor column on the row (proposer / applier / requester / identifier / createdBy) — and re-run the same exclusion inside the EXECUTION rule, not only the predicate.
nodes.artefact: GroovyPredicate + the paired GroovyExecutionRule; requires identity columns on the entity filled from service.security.user().email
nodes.antiPattern: Asserting the state inside the reusable "may this person approve?" predicate — one project did, and because the rule was also reused by Reverse (valid from a different state) every reverse button on nine document types was permanently hidden, with no error.

nodes.name: Every nav item carries its target page's roleGroupAccessors — including the console links
nodes.rule: Both projects that did Phase 6 gate all 55 / all 44 nav links with `publicReadAccess:false, authenticatedUserAccess:false` and the same group map as the page, and gate Rules/Contexts/Workflows/Database/Business Logic/Settings/… to Author, Developer and the customer-admin persona, turning the platform console into a product.
nodes.artefact: virtualPlugins "Nct left nav" → site.kicker.plugin → properties.modelGroups.stringValue → pagesModel[].roleAccess
nodes.antiPattern: Setting roleAccess on a nav item while leaving publicReadAccess:true — the check short-circuits on public and the ticks do nothing; or gating a link to stale template persona names, which appears in 3 of 4 projects on the Home/Users links and hides them from every real user.

nodes.name: Hide a number from a persona by gating the field node AND its label, and omitting the column
nodes.rule: 204 nodes in one project — 64 labels + 54 text fields + dropdowns + datepickers + 6 KPI charts — carry their own roleAccess granting view only to the management persona (currency, exchange rate, unit price, unit cost, line/total amount), while the matching crud.table simply leaves the money columns out of columnSettings.
nodes.artefact: roleAccess on dynaform.form.*.plugin / nct.label.plugin / chart.js.plugin nodes + crud.table columnSettings
nodes.antiPattern: Gating the field but not its label, leaving a caption over nothing; or expecting a per-placement grant on a linked common component's page-local stub to work (it reads the shared node).

nodes.name: Three permission tiers in roleGroupAccessors, and never edit without view
nodes.rule: Authoring groups get view+edit+advancedEdit, a working persona gets view+edit, an oversight persona gets view only — 967 grants follow this in the two projects that gated by persona.
nodes.artefact: siteMapPage.roleAccess.roleGroupAccessors[<group>] = {view, edit, advancedEdit}
nodes.antiPattern: `{"edit": true, "view": false}` — the render check reads `view`, so the persona whose job was user and role-group administration could not open a single console page.

nodes.name: Charts, pager totals, and scheduler-run rules are outside every gate
nodes.rule: 0 of 87 charts in the best-gated project apply its branch scope (SQL has no access to service.security); 241 of 244 generated `find` methods call `count()` with no filter so totalElements leaks the unscoped row count; and all 43 schedulers across the four projects run with serviceUserId:null, so hasAnyRoleGroup is false and a reused scoped fetch rule returns nothing.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin properties.Javascript + rep-objects.queries · dynamic-cruds find GROOVY script · rep-objects.schedulers serviceUserId
nodes.antiPattern: A branch-scoped case list sitting on a page whose dashboard totals every branch; and reusing a scoped fetch rule from a scheduler, which takes the !hasAnyRoleGroup branch and the fail-closed sentinel and returns zero rows for ever.

nodes.name: Do not reimplement authorisation in business tables when the role API misbehaves
nodes.rule: One project rebuilt permissions on system_settings rows plus a comma-separated users.role_groups mirror after hasAnyRoleGroup answered false for everyone on its deployment; its own comments record the default being open, the mirror recording a Worker as Manager/Author/Owner under the wrong id, jsonb values arriving as Jackson nodes so every read silently fell back to the hardcoded default, and the restricted user being unable to read the settings table that was meant to restrict them.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin studio rules calling service.crud.system_settings_cruid
nodes.antiPattern: `def restrict = false` as the default of an authorisation check; an unreadable or empty config widening a privilege; a role mirror column in business data.

nodes.name: A rule opens the case; the worklist never does
nodes.rule: All 15 start sites are EXECUTION_RULEs (10 register lifecycle actions, 4 scheduler sweeps, 1 user-task action of another case); userStartProcessActions is empty on 14 of 14 real worklists and no project built a start form.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE wired as a crud-table action's onBeforeCompleteRuleIdentifier / a ScheduleDto's actionRuleIdentifier / a userAction's onBeforeUserTaskCompleteRuleIdentifier
nodes.antiPattern: A: 5 authored diagrams, zero starters, zero worklists — each workflow's identifier appears exactly once in the whole export (its own definition).

nodes.name: The three-part document-action start block
nodes.rule: Status gate (only DRAFT may submit) → case-already-open gate (the write-back column empty, and/or caseSubjectId already in attrs) → start, then write the returned process id back onto the row — in that order, 10 times over two projects.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE behind a crud-table action + a dedicated `set<X>Process` SQL method
nodes.antiPattern: Starting before the write-back column is checked, or marking before starting — the latter is the duplicate storm with no way to tell the copies apart.

nodes.name: Claim by timestamp, mark by identifier, repair by age, release on re-entry
nodes.rule: process_started_at (claim) + process_identifier (mark) + process_start_count, with findClaimedWithoutCase/releaseCaseClaim keyed on a 5-minute age, a countCaseCandidates gate that counts the repairable backlog too, and an endCase that clears both columns when a terminal branch allows the subject to come back.
nodes.artefact: 4–6 hand-authored SQL methods on the subject CRUD (returnsArray:false, RETURNING *) + an EXECUTION_RULE repair sweep called first inside the opening rule
nodes.antiPattern: C's one-column 'CLAIMING' sentinel: atomic but undateable, so a crash between claim and start pins the row for ever and no repair query can find it — and C shipped no repair sweep for any of its three.

nodes.name: The bind/publish service task before every human step
nodes.rule: Node 1 after the start event is always a bind rule that resolves the subject id under every alias, reads the record from the database and copies its display fields into prefixed GLOBAL attrs; two of three projects repeat it before each user task, and every rule that changes the record republishes the attributes it changed.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE named `Bind <Entity>` / `Publish the case fields — <Entity>`, first in the serviceTask's flowable:rule CSV; feeds a 20-control all-GLOBAL read-only card form
nodes.antiPattern: A binds the entity's own 100 %-CRUD-scope form group as the task form with no bind rule at all — the card renders blank inside a case.

nodes.name: A gateway's default is where the process lands when it could not tell
nodes.rule: Nine of ten gateways carry a question for a name, one bare branch named in `default`, a `name` on every branch, and a predicate that re-reads the record; the disagreement is what `default` points at — rework (item), terminate (C), or the happy path (importer) — and only the first two are safe, because a predicate answers false for every reason it could not decide.
nodes.artefact: exclusiveGateway `default` attribute + a bare sequenceFlow + a PREDICATE that does service.crud.<alias>.get(id)
nodes.antiPattern: A: an exclusiveGateway named 'Override required?' with ONE outgoing flow, no condition and no default — a diamond that decides nothing. And D pointing `default` at 'raise the follow-up document' / 'post the movement'.

nodes.name: INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING * as the second atomic primitive
nodes.rule: For 'announce this exactly once' the claim is an INSERT against a partial unique index (subject, clock, escalation point), with an explicit deleted=false in the VALUES so the row falls inside the index and returnsArray:false so 'already warned' comes back as Groovy null.
nodes.artefact: SQL CRUD method + `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … WHERE (deleted = false)` in project-db.dump
nodes.antiPattern: A's findAll(2000)+Groovy .find dedupe on an alert's message text, and B's audit-entry watermark scan — both read-then-write, both O(rows) per tick.

nodes.name: Warn → register → open a case, at descending cadence
nodes.rule: Half-hourly warnings at policy-configured percentages of the SLA window (unique-index guarded), hourly breach records into an exception register (unique-index guarded), weekday-morning case opening from the register (claim guarded) — three schedules, three primitives, one clock family.
nodes.artefact: 3 ScheduleDto + 3 EXECUTION_RULEs + a deadline-policy CRUD (duration_value/unit/escalation_points) + a holiday table + a byte-identical copy-pasted policy prelude
nodes.antiPattern: Collapsing all rungs into one rule, or encoding a rung's deadline as the cron period.

nodes.name: The gate is the candidate query with LIMIT 1
nodes.rule: Ten of sixteen gated schedules gate on the same statement the action pages through, with rowsInPage:1 (or a dedicated count* method), ending in an explicit `return <Boolean>` — so the gate can never drift from the work.
nodes.artefact: PREDICATE rule as ScheduleDto.predicateIdentifier
nodes.antiPattern: A: 27 schedulers, 0 gates, all enabled:true, all serviceUserEmail null — every tick runs the full action from the moment of import.

nodes.name: One workflow, one process group, one worklist page, 3–6 GLOBAL columns, 2 index entries
nodes.rule: 14 of 14 real worklists: a dedicated siteMapPage, a settings[] mirror named after the node's uniqueIdentifier, a filter form, exactly two indexSettings feeding a two-clause ignoreNull filterExpression, empty userStartProcessActions, and at most one global action (the read-only viewer).
nodes.artefact: process.table.pluin node model + rep-objects.settings[] {type:"ProcessTable"} mirror + a business-group quick link
nodes.antiPattern: A ships only the seeded placeholder node, on a leftover page, pointing at one of its five dead workflows and at a SEEDED process group; C carries 120 orphan ProcessTable mirrors against 8 nodes.

nodes.name: Worklist columns read the published GLOBAL attrs, not the crud snapshot
nodes.rule: 24 GLOBAL columns vs 10 CRUD across the corpus; the CRUD ones read the document snapshot the starting rule passed and go stale the moment a service task writes the row — while the same project's bind rule already republishes those values as attrs.
nodes.artefact: columnSettings[].scope on the process.table model + the prefixed case* attrs the bind rule setAttr's
nodes.antiPattern: C's all-CRUD columns; and note the flip side — businessKey and status as GLOBAL columns are a FEATURE (they answer off the process row) that B uses deliberately for 'Case' and 'Case state'.

nodes.name: The five user-task action shapes, and the gate/decision separation
nodes.rule: Decide-with-a-form (36/47), direct advance (4), read-only viewer (completeUserTask:off + submitForm:false + formInModal, reusing the bind rule as its complete rule), reject-paired-with-approve on the same task and the same predicate, and create-a-child-record; the predicate always answers 'may this actor act now?', never 'what was decided'.
nodes.artefact: flowable:userActions ActionDto on a bpmn:UserTask
nodes.antiPattern: A's 10 actions carry no predicate, no complete rule and no icon; and validationRuleIdentifiers is unused in all 47 — preconditions are throws inside the complete rule.

nodes.name: A sweep must not write a field a running case's gateway routes on
nodes.rule: No rule can end a case (service.workflow exposes only start), so a sweep that changes the routing column steers a case a human is standing in; sweeps write annotation columns (escalated, attempts, last_chased_at) and the case writes state — and the postpone/park wait is a scheduler plus a terminal branch, because there is no timer event.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE behind a ScheduleDto + a `reopen`/`endCase` SQL method pair
nodes.antiPattern: Writing POSTPONED from the escalation sweep: the open case's gateway would then take the postpone branch, close with no follow-up document, and leave the claim set for ever.

nodes.name: Process key must be Process_<workflow identifier>
nodes.rule: Two of four projects shipped every workflow keyed <process id="Process_1"> — one of them five DEPLOYED workflows on one key, which Flowable treats as a single target with a shared deployment version.
nodes.artefact: the <process id> attribute in bpmnContent
nodes.antiPattern: A (6×Process_1) and B (5×Process_1, all deployed).

nodes.name: The start-call document: three levels, prefixed attrs, four options always passed
nodes.rule: contextDataMap keyed by context IDENTIFIER → crudDataMap by ALIAS → nested camelCase row under value; root attrs carry the binding under every name later steps resolve by plus prefixed case* display fields; groupIdentifier, roleGroups (2 groups) and businessKey (the human reference) are passed at 15/15 sites, owner at 12/15, emails at 0/15.
nodes.artefact: service.workflow.start(wfId, document, options) inside an EXECUTION_RULE
nodes.antiPattern: Forwarding [contextDataMap: contextDataMap] — null in every headless caller, which starts an empty process and still returns a process identifier.

nodes.name: The sanctioned exception: an onBeforeUserTaskStart loader for a CRUD-scoped task form
nodes.rule: To reuse a rich CRUD approval form inside a case, a never-throwing start rule reloads the document, PUTs it into the crud data map and RETURNS it (so whichever path the build honours, the card fills) — 10 of 10 form actions in one project.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE as ActionDto.onBeforeUserTaskStartRuleIdentifier
nodes.antiPattern: Letting that rule throw — an erroring start rule stops the form opening at all, so a blank card beats no card; and the try/catch-everything discipline it forces makes real failures invisible.

nodes.name: The document-register action set
nodes.rule: One fixed table of ten actions — Create/Edit/View as form actions, every state transition as a direct action with its own predicate and execution rule — repeated verbatim for each document entity.
nodes.artefact: crud.table.plugin properties.model.stringValue → createActions.actions[] / editActions.actions[]
nodes.antiPattern: Putting a record-scoped action (View, Post, Approve) in `createActions`: it has no row context and never appears as a row action. Only the bare Create belongs there.

nodes.name: The action predicate hides, roleAccess blocks, the rule throws
nodes.rule: Three layered gates: `predicateIdentifier` hides the button, the form/landing page's `roleAccess.roleGroupAccessors` blocks the URL, and the execution rule re-asserts the same precondition with a throw.
nodes.artefact: action.predicateIdentifier + siteMapPage.roleAccess + the onBeforeComplete EXECUTION rule
nodes.antiPattern: Relying on the visibility predicate alone: the landing is reachable by URL with ?group=&settingsName=&actionId=&crudId= — every parameter is visible to anyone who once had the button.

nodes.name: One state-free shared authorization predicate, called by every Can-<Verb>
nodes.rule: A project-wide PREDICATE that answers only 'may this person approve?' (role + four-eyes), invoked as `service.rule("…") as boolean` from each entity's per-verb predicate, which owns the state assertion.
nodes.artefact: rules[] ruleType=PREDICATE, referenced from action.predicateIdentifier and from mapping predicates
nodes.antiPattern: Asserting caller-specific state inside the shared rule. A live instance added `status=='SUBMITTED'` to the shared approver rule, which made Can Reverse (POSTED/CLOSED) logically impossible and silently hid every Reverse button on eleven entities.

nodes.name: The approval twin (fork by state + role, not by actionId)
nodes.rule: A second form in the same group — a field-for-field copy of the main form with alwaysProhibited:true on everything the approver may not touch — routed by a narrow `status + shared-approver` predicate placed above the default pair.
nodes.artefact: formGroups[].predicateFormMapping.mapping[] + a second forms[] entry + a second form page
nodes.antiPattern: `return service.actionId == '<uuid>'` forks: zero live uses, uuid-coupled, and unbound on the workflow branch so the same group reached from a worklist silently falls through to the fallback form.

nodes.name: Mandatory = alwaysMandatory + localized messages + the red asterisk in slot HTML
nodes.rule: 356 of 356 mandatory controls in four projects pair `alwaysMandatory:true` (+ a three-locale mandatoryValidationMessages map) with a `*` inside the slot's flex header — an exact 1:1, never one without the other.
nodes.artefact: control settings.alwaysMandatory / settings.mandatoryValidationMessages + the gen_slot_* nct.html.plugin `html` property
nodes.antiPattern: Setting `alwaysMandatory` without the slot asterisk (field validates but looks optional) or without `mandatoryValidationMessages` (114 live controls fall back to the generic "{fieldName} is required" in a three-language app).

nodes.name: Form-level VALIDATION_RULE: always addFieldError AND addError
nodes.rule: Cross-field checks live in `forms[].validators`; every finding is reported twice — `addFieldError(<exact settings.name>, m)` marks the control and `addError(m)` is what actually renders the sentence.
nodes.artefact: rules[] ruleType=VALIDATION_RULE / executor=GroovyValidationRule, referenced from forms[].validators[]
nodes.antiPattern: Title-casing the label in the rule. Live: `addFieldError("Liability Conclusion"…)` against a control named `Liability conclusion`, and `"Liability Justification"` against `Justification` — 4 of 4 targets miss, the messages vanish, and the user sees a bare "Validation failed".

nodes.name: One cross-cutting validator attached to every document form, self-locating via a READERS probe
nodes.rule: A single VALIDATION_RULE (e.g. 'the accounting period is locked') attached to 14 forms, which walks a list of `[alias, { context.<ctx>.<alias>.data.get() }]` closures inside try/catch to find whichever document is actually in scope.
nodes.artefact: rules[] VALIDATION_RULE referenced from many forms[].validators[]
nodes.antiPattern: Writing one near-identical validator per entity — 11 copies to keep in sync, and the settings lookup duplicated in each.

nodes.name: GLOBAL + alwaysProhibited echo band on a form reached from both a table row and a worklist task
nodes.rule: Read-only header fields whose `fieldExpression` deliberately matches BOTH the parent CRUD's column name and the attr the workflow bind rule publishes, so one control reads correctly on the CRUD-forced path and the attrs path.
nodes.artefact: control settings {scope:GLOBAL, alwaysProhibited:true, fieldExpression:<column name>}
nodes.antiPattern: GLOBAL *inputs* on a table-only form read with `context.data.getAttr(...)`: live instance writes '' into the CRUD method, a COALESCE update keeps the old value, and the toast still says success.

nodes.name: The `_rid` closure — resolve the row id from context, attrs, or a published attr
nodes.rule: A closure tried in every predicate and rule: context row → `attrs.get('_crudEntityId')` → `context.data.getAttr(alias+'Id')`, then caches the winner back with setAttr so the next rule finds it; the row is reloaded with `service.crud.<alias>.get(id)` when the context copy is thin.
nodes.artefact: PREDICATE and EXECUTION rule bodies
nodes.antiPattern: Reading only `context.<ctx>.<alias>.data.get()`: returns null/throws on the workflow path, so the same rule cannot serve a row action and a user task.

nodes.name: The state field: read-only dropdown, static initial default, help bubble naming the buttons
nodes.rule: Every document form renders `status` as a rule-driven dropdown with alwaysProhibited:true and defaultValue 'DRAFT', plus an nct.help.plugin in the same slot explaining that the status moves with the register's buttons.
nodes.artefact: dynaform.form.rimm.drop.down.field.plugin settings + sibling nct.help.plugin helpSettings
nodes.antiPattern: Leaving the state field editable (the user types a state the transition rules never validated) or omitting it entirely (the user cannot see why the buttons changed).

nodes.name: Cascade by repainting form.parsis, not by chasing slots
nodes.rule: The dependent-dropdown event targets the form's own `form.parsis` nct.parsis.plugin with an empty executionRuleIdentifiers list — one mapping repaints every dependent field on the form in one ajax round trip.
nodes.artefact: control settings.eventComponentMappings[] {eventName:'change', componentIdentifier:<uniqueIdentifier of form.parsis>}
nodes.antiPattern: Per-slot targets on a form with several dependent fields: one mapping per target, and the wiring silently rots when a field moves slot (validate only WARNs on a dead componentIdentifier).

nodes.name: Pick an existing record and prefill header + child lines in one event
nodes.rule: A `change` event on the parent picker runs one EXECUTION rule that mutates `context.<ctx>.<alias>.data` in place (including `row.lines = [...]` built from the parent's line query) and then repaints form.parsis.
nodes.artefact: settings.eventComponentMappings[].executionRuleIdentifiers[0] → an EXECUTION rule
nodes.antiPattern: Letting the rule throw. Every context touch must be inside try/catch with an early `return null` — `.data` throws when the context has no entry for the crud and `.get()` throws when the entry is empty, and a throwing rule aborts the refresh with no visible change.

nodes.name: View / Back — the read-only drill-down action
nodes.rule: `direct:false` + `submitForm:false` + the same formGroupIdentifier + no complete rule, icon pe-7s-look, button label Back (or Open/Close); the submit button becomes a Back that skips validation, rules and writes.
nodes.artefact: editActions.actions[] entry
nodes.antiPattern: `direct:false` + `submitForm:false` + `onBeforeCompleteRuleIdentifier` — a button that returns to the table and does nothing. Zero live instances; the docs' warning is correct and obeyed.

nodes.name: The List sub-form action template
nodes.rule: Add(direct:'off', pe-7s-plus, button Save) / Edit(direct:'off', pe-7s-pen, Save) / Delete(direct:'on', pe-7s-trash), subforms:[{id:Add}], formIdByActionId:{Add:Add, Edit:Add}, and one child dynaform.list.item.plugin whose identifier IS the Add action id.
nodes.artefact: dynaform.form.list.field.plugin settings.createNewActions / userActions / subforms / formIdByActionId + child dynaform.list.item.plugin
nodes.antiPattern: Writing `direct: true/false` (boolean) on a List action — a List uses the UserTask-shaped ActionDto where `direct` is the STRING "on"/"off"; a boolean is ignored and the Delete opens a form.

nodes.name: One landing per group, form page as its sibling, layout Main, alias on both
nodes.rule: placeFormsNextToLanding:true, formGroupsPageIdentifier:null, the group's own landing page and the form page both children of the CRUD-table page with unique top-level aliases and both plugins inside the html.plugin "Layout" chrome.
nodes.artefact: formGroups[] + forms[] + the two siteMapPages
nodes.antiPattern: Pointing a group's contentPageIdentifier at the baseline system `Landing`: 38 live groups do, and that page ships authenticatedUserAccess:false with admin/author-only accessors, so an ordinary clerk is access-denied on Create/Edit while the author never sees it.

nodes.name: The unfinished action — no localizedNames, no persist rule
nodes.rule: An action carrying only {id, icon, formGroupIdentifier, direct:false} (sometimes with a legacy flat `name` the deserializer drops) renders a blank menu entry whose Save writes nothing, and every gate stays green.
nodes.artefact: createActions.actions[] / editActions.actions[]
nodes.antiPattern: The CRUD ActionDto has no `name` field — only localizedNames/localizedButtonNames maps — and there is no built-in create/update; both omissions are silent at import, at coverage and at crud verify.

nodes.name: Hand-written conditional validation: try `v`, then the path-specific fallback
nodes.rule: The two non-generated conditionalValidations entries skip the generated scope preamble and read `try { raw = v }` then fall back to `context.data.getAttr('<field>')` (dual-reach GLOBAL control) or `context.currentData?.getField('<field>', <Type>.class)` (control inside a list-item sub-form).
nodes.artefact: control settings.conditionalValidations[] + a PREDICATE rule
nodes.antiPattern: Trusting the generated preamble on a form whose opening path differs from the persisted scope — the CRUD preamble returns null on a task form and the attrs preamble returns null on a table form, and a body starting `return v == null ||` then rejects a field the user did fill in.

nodes.name: Two-column grid, one-column rows for the wide things
nodes.rule: gen_row (nct.html.plugin, `<div class="row">` + two `col-md-6`) → gen_col (nct.parsis.plugin) → gen_slot (nct.html.plugin, `<div class="mb-3">` + label + optional help + field); textarea, List and totals get their own one-column rows.
nodes.artefact: the form page's form.parsis subtree
nodes.antiPattern: A slot whose `html` references a `<plugin id=…>` that does not match a child node's identifier — the only real constraint; both the hex batch tag and a human batch tag (gen_slot_<entity><nn>_<c>_<i>) work, and the human tag makes the export diffable.

nodes.name: The canonical method set and its order band
nodes.rule: find(-1,GROOVY) findAll(0) count(1) get(2) create(3) update(4) delete(5) undelete(6), with document line-helpers occupying 6-10 and pushing undelete to 11; lifecycle transitions 20-29; derived/query methods 30-39.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json cruds[].methods[] — methodName/methodOrder/methodType/returnsArray
nodes.antiPattern: C places the SQL line helpers at 3-8 and the GROOVY create/update at 9/10, breaking the universal 3=create/4=update/5=delete reflex; A leaves 65 of 160 CRUDs with filterFields that findAll has no parameter for, so the filter control is silently inert.

nodes.name: Five entity kinds, five method sets
nodes.rule: 188 flat registers, 25 register+lifecycle/queue, 19 header+lines documents, 12 read-only report CRUDs (find/findAll/count ONLY, findAll is an inline derived query, count wraps it in SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (...) rpt), ~3 utility CRUDs with no CRUD verbs at all.
nodes.artefact: whole-CRUD shape decision, made before any method is written
nodes.antiPattern: Giving every entity the same method set. A read-only report CRUD with create/update/delete carries three methods nobody can call, and a header+lines document with only the base eight silently loses its lines on every save.

nodes.name: Text-anchor every optional filter
nodes.rule: Three interchangeable idioms — `col IS NOT DISTINCT FROM COALESCE(NULLIF(:x,''), col)`, `col ILIKE COALESCE('%'||NULLIF(:x,'')||'%', col)`, `COALESCE(CAST(NULLIF(:x,'') AS uuid|boolean|timestamptz), col)` — all anchoring the slot to text with a literal '' so an absent/blank param is typed and means 'no filter'; the anchor, not the operator, is the load-bearing part.
nodes.artefact: findAll + count method scripts; count repeats findAll's WHERE verbatim minus the `t.` alias and paging
nodes.antiPattern: A writes `(CAST(:assignedTo AS varchar) IS NULL OR t.assigned_to = CAST(:assignedTo AS varchar))` on findAll while its count declares ZERO parameters — rows come back filtered, totalElements reports the whole table.

nodes.name: count is findAll's WHERE minus paging, and never has exactly one parameter
nodes.rule: count.parameters == findAll.parameters − {rowsInPage,pageNumber} in 240/241 CRUDs; 0 of 244 has a one-parameter count because filter sets are always 0 or >=2, which structurally immunises against the single-slot positional-binding trap.
nodes.artefact: count method parameters + script
nodes.antiPattern: Writing count's WHERE by hand. It drifts from findAll on the first new filter, and the pager then reports a total that does not match the rows — a defect no gate catches because both statements are valid SQL.

nodes.name: Soft delete as a five-part package
nodes.rule: delete = `UPDATE t SET deleted=true, modification_time=now() WHERE id=CAST(:id AS uuid) RETURNING *`; undelete is the inverse at order 6; `AND deleted=false` on findAll AND count AND get; `deleted` is NEVER a dtoField (0 of 81); child/line tables stay HARD delete with no undelete; uniqueness survives via `ON CONFLICT (k) WHERE deleted=false`.
nodes.artefact: delete/undelete methods + the read triad's WHERE + dtoFields omission
nodes.antiPattern: A hard-deletes all 160 CRUDs with no `deleted` column at all, so a mis-click is unrecoverable and any inbound FK makes delete fail outright.

nodes.name: The shape-agnostic Groovy prelude for document orchestrators
nodes.rule: A byte-identical closure block (_size/_at/_num/_txt/_ref/_lineNo/_id/_fk) heads every GROOVY create/update so the same method works whether `lines` arrives as a Groovy List of Maps (rule caller) or a Jackson ArrayNode of ObjectNodes (form caller); insertLine is then called with an explicit hand-built map, never the raw node.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json GROOVY create/update scripts on header+lines CRUDs (ruleIdentifier REQUIRED)
nodes.antiPattern: C writes `lines.eachWithIndex { ln, i -> new LinkedHashMap(ln instanceof Map ? ln : [:]) }` — a Jackson ObjectNode is iterable but is NOT a java.util.Map, so every line a form submits becomes an EMPTY map: the header saves, the lines vanish, nothing errors.

nodes.name: FK handling: pick nested or flat per project, declare both parameter spellings always
nodes.rule: Business FK either flat (`counterpartyId` + sibling `counterpartyName`, single-underscore alias) or nested (`counterparty` as ObjectNode, `jN.id AS "counterparty__id"/__code/__name` triple) — 2 projects each way; but every document CRUD in all three non-scaffold projects declares BOTH `<ref>__id` AND plain `<ref>` as parameters, and reconciles them with `_fk()` before calling the header helper.
nodes.artefact: dtoFields fieldName/fieldType + findAll/get SELECT aliases + create/update parameters[]
nodes.antiPattern: Doc 11 says the bare `<ref>` FK field is 'a deliberate exception, not the flat default' — two projects use it as their default for all business FKs. Also: `_id$` is not proof of an FK (tax_id), and machine-written back-references (reversal_id, corrected_from_id, source_doc_id, polymorphic reference_id, self-refs) stay flat even in nested projects.

nodes.name: Quote every camelCase SELECT alias
nodes.rule: Postgres folds unquoted identifiers — including column aliases — to lower case, so `j2.id AS case__id` reaches mapRow as `case__id` and surfaces as `{case:{...}}`, silently blanking every consumer bound to `case.name`; write `AS "<ref>__<col>"` whenever either part has an upper-case letter.
nodes.artefact: findAll/get SELECT alias list in dynamic-cruds.json (and the mirrored paired query)
nodes.antiPattern: C ships 202 unquoted camelCase aliases across 38 methods while its own branches.json binds fieldExpression "case.name"/"case.id" 24 times; D ships 6. B quotes all 132 of its camelCase aliases and leaves the all-lowercase ones bare — the correct discipline.

nodes.name: Stamp audit columns in SQL, never expose them as parameters
nodes.rule: JPA preamble creation_time/modification_time/created_by/modified_by: create writes `gen_random_uuid(), now(), now(), :created_by, :modified_by`; update writes `modification_time = now()` unconditionally outside any COALESCE (72/72 creates and 69/72 updates in the three JPA-style projects).
nodes.artefact: create/update/createHeader/updateHeader SQL
nodes.antiPattern: A declares created_at/updated_at as ordinary parameters and writes `updated_at = COALESCE(:updated_at, updated_at)` in all 160 updates — no form ever submits them, so updated_at never changes and the audit column is a lie.

nodes.name: Lifecycle transitions are guarded SQL UPDATEs, and the state flip goes last
nodes.rule: `UPDATE t SET status='POSTED', posted_at=now(), posted_by=COALESCE(NULLIF(:actor,''),posted_by), modification_time=now() WHERE id=CAST(:id AS uuid) AND status='SUBMITTED' RETURNING *` — the `AND status='<previous>'` clause IS the state machine (0 rows, no exception, no double posting); the calling rule pre-checks the same state to give the user a sentence, then runs validate → stamp → recompute → re-get → side effects → flip LAST.
nodes.artefact: lifecycle SQL methods + the action rule that calls them
nodes.antiPattern: D guards only 3 of its 25 transitions — purchaseOrder.send/confirm/reject/close/cancel all fire from any state, so a stale tab can re-post a closed order.

nodes.name: The queue / claim / reap method family for scheduler-driven work
nodes.rule: find<X>Candidates (paged, unclaimed, oldest first) + count<X>Candidates + claimFor<X> (atomic guarded UPDATE; RETURNING null == somebody else has it) + set<X>Process + find<Claimed>Without<X> (stale reaper, >5 min) + release<X>Claim + end<X>; two marker columns (process_started_at + process_identifier + process_start_count) beat one column with a 'CLAIMING' sentinel.
nodes.artefact: extra SQL methods on a queue-bearing CRUD, called from a cron rule
nodes.antiPattern: C's single-column sentinel form cannot distinguish 'claimed but the process never started' from 'never claimed', which is exactly what the reaper needs.

nodes.name: The auto-find paging wrapper — one script, 240 times
nodes.rule: GROOVY find at order -1 with ruleIdentifier/queryIdentifier/contextIdentifiers/returnFields all null, the fallback body (`param ?: [:]`, `.count()` with no arg) returning {content,totalElements,totalPages,pageNumber}, and declaring the SAME parameter list as findAll.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json methods[] where methodName == find
nodes.antiPattern: A has 6 variant-B finds (ruleIdentifier set, contextIdentifiers []); five have bodies byte-identical to the auto-find and buy nothing but a Groovy execution per page-load, and the sixth reads service.security and then ignores the result. Row scope belongs in a table fetch rule, not in find.

nodes.name: Row scope in a table fetch rule, threaded through both findAll and count
nodes.rule: A `Branch Scope Filter - <Entity>` rule reads `attrs` (NOT param) into a filter map, forwards paging and user filters, then writes the scope key LAST so a crafted client filter cannot widen it; it fails CLOSED with an all-zero uuid, and the scope key is a declared parameter of BOTH findAll and count (12/12).
nodes.artefact: rep-objects.json rules[] (table fetch rule) + a branchScopeId/branchId filter param on findAll and count
nodes.antiPattern: Scoping inside the CRUD's own `find` (variant B) — the only project that tried it computed the role check and never applied it, and its count declared no scope parameter at all.

nodes.name: Method script and paired query must stay one artefact
nodes.rule: Every SQL method has a query named exactly `crud_<alias>_<method>` with `hidden: null` and a body byte-identical to the method script after the {name,type}<->:name transform — 815/815 in the three disciplined projects.
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json methods[].queryIdentifier <-> rep-objects.json queries[]
nodes.antiPattern: A: 131 methods whose paired query carries a NEWER SELECT than the running script (the fix went into the wrong copy, and merely opening the editor will revert the running one), 126 methods cross-wired to ANOTHER CRUD's query records, and 150 orphan crud_* queries.

nodes.name: recompute / stamp / version methods
nodes.rule: recomputeTotals rolls line SUMs into the header; stampLines freezes master data onto `*_snapshot` columns at posting time so history cannot move; nextVersion / supersedeOthers / activate(compute derived cols) / findActiveByItem manage versioned parameter rows.
nodes.artefact: extra SQL methods, methodOrder 30+, taking only :id
nodes.antiPattern: Computing a total in the UI or in a rule instead of in one SQL UPDATE, and joining to master data at read time instead of stamping a snapshot at posting time — the first drifts between screens, the second silently rewrites history when somebody renames a row.

nodes.name: The source block is scrubbed, and an unresolvable sourceIdentifier is a dead CRUD
nodes.rule: sourcePassword is null in 244/244 CRUDs and 5/5 sources — import takes live credentials from rep-objects.json.sources[] by sourceIdentifier; fill the other seven fields identically on every CRUD, keep dbType "POISTGRESQL" and sourceType "INTERNAL".
nodes.artefact: dynamic-cruds.json cruds[].source* + rep-objects.json sources[]
nodes.antiPattern: A has one CRUD pointing at a second source whose UUID appears in no sources[] record — nothing supplies credentials on import and every SQL method on it fails at connect time.

nodes.name: The html plugin is a layout host, not a component
nodes.rule: 99.3 % of nct.html.plugin nodes across four projects are classic layout wrapping <plugin> children; three of the four projects contain zero studio components, and 645 nodes carry the noise literal {"docs":[],"libs":[],"css":{"byTheme":{}},"scripts":[]} that makes grepping for real components useless.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin · properties.html + properties.studioModel
nodes.antiPattern: Shipping the empty studioModel on auto-generated gen_row_*/gen_slot_* nodes (226+115+109 in one project alone) — it buys nothing and hides the real components.

nodes.name: A project kit shipped once as a vendored studio library
nodes.rule: Cross-cutting component behaviour lives in one JS_CLASSIC file at tenant-files/studio/<kit>/<kit>.js declared as libs[{name,globalVar}] and reached as ctx.libs.<kit>, so it exists once instead of being copy-pasted into every screen.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.libs[] + tenant-files/studio/app-kit/app-kit.js (9.6 kB, kind JS_CLASSIC, globalVar "appkit")
nodes.antiPattern: The same project then copy-pasted its ~200-line helper preamble (q/esc/errText/pick/say/bind/action/L/applyLocale) into all 22 components — ≈4 400 duplicated lines — and its own post-mortem records three incomplete defect sweeps caused by it. The preamble belonged in the kit.

nodes.name: Breadcrumb-by-proxy — mirror an in-page button into the title bar
nodes.rule: Instead of re-declaring page actions with ctx.breadcrumb.set(), a library hides the screen's existing button (display:none, never remove), forwards el.click(), mirrors label/disabled/hidden with a MutationObserver, and resolves the spinner on the FIRST `disabled` mutation after the click — not on disabled===false, because a screen can re-enable and re-disable in one synchronous block.
nodes.artefact: app-kit.js `actions(ctx, spec)` + `waitIdle(el, maxMs)`; call sites in 20 of 22 components
nodes.antiPattern: Reading the final `disabled` state in the observer callback: deleting the last row re-enables then re-disables synchronously, the promise never resolves, and the blockUI overlay covers the screen for the full 30 s timeout.

nodes.name: Top-level try{} per script — error UI plus per-script block scope
nodes.rule: Wrapping each script in `try { … } catch (err) { <primary container>.textContent = 'Script error: ' + …; console.error(…) }` turns a silently dead component into a visible message AND block-scopes that script's const/let, so two scripts of one component can both declare `const BOUND`, `esc`, `L`, `q` without the compile error 24d warns about.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code — line 1 and last line of all 24 scripts
nodes.antiPattern: Relying on the shared scope to pass helpers between scripts: with the try{} wrapper they are invisible to each other, which is why every script re-declares the whole preamble. Share through ctx.libs.<kit> or ctx.api instead.

nodes.name: Synchronous script body, load() launched and never awaited
nodes.rule: Define → bind → declare breadcrumb actions → `load().catch(e => primaryContainer.innerHTML = errorRow)`; the only await lives inside load(), so there is no "first await" and every ctx.on/ctx.onCleanup registration is structurally safe against a mid-fetch Wicket re-render.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code — tail of all 22 main scripts
nodes.antiPattern: `const d = await ctx.callRule(...); ctx.on('x', reload);` — after a teardown ctx.on() silently refuses and ctx.onCleanup(fn) runs fn immediately, both with a clean console.

nodes.name: Author the loading and empty state in properties.html
nodes.rule: `Loading…` is server-rendered and already painted before the script runs, which removes the need for the paint() macrotask yield before the first blocking bridge call (21 of 22 components carry no paint() helper at all).
nodes.artefact: properties.html.stringValue + css `.app-empty{color:var(--app-mut);text-align:center;padding:18px}`
nodes.antiPattern: A table that cannot load leaving the static "Loading…" in place while the reason goes to a message strip elsewhere on the page — the operator sees a table loading forever. A table that cannot load must say so IN the table (`tableFail(sel, cols, e)`).

nodes.name: Client-side paging over one fetch, with the row ceiling in the rule
nodes.rule: Not one of the 22 components pages on the server: the rule sets `def page = [rowsInPage: 2000, pageNumber: 0]`, returns everything in one envelope, and JS filters, sorts and slices in memory — because the bridge is a synchronous page-freezing XHR and every server page-turn would freeze the tab.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION rule `<Screen> Screen Data (Studio)` + `const PAGE_SIZE = 25` client pager built by render()
nodes.antiPattern: Server-paging a 200-row table: each page turn, sort click and search keystroke becomes a whole-tab freeze. Above ~2 000 rows the trade flips and 24c's contract wins — but the ceiling belongs in the rule either way.

nodes.name: safe{} per source in a multi-entity fetch rule
nodes.rule: `def safe = { cl -> try { return cl() ?: [] } catch (Throwable t) { __trace << ('src: ' + t.getMessage()); return [] } }` wraps every service.crud read so one broken table degrades one region instead of blanking the console, and the reason rides back in a `trace[]` field of the [ok, trace, locale, …lists] envelope.
nodes.artefact: EXECUTION_RULE named `<Screen> … (Studio)` — 51 distinct rules, all EXECUTION, all ACTIVE
nodes.antiPattern: One try/catch around the whole rule: a single missing table makes the entire eight-entity screen throw, and the operator gets one unactionable exception instead of seven working regions.

nodes.name: errText — normalising the opaque ExecutionError envelope
nodes.rule: A rule that throws can come back as `{"ok":false,"error":"[…ExecuteResponse$ExecutionError@33872ff2]"}` — the field is present and its contents are a Java identity hash; test what you are about to return with /ExecutionError|ExecuteResponse\$|@[0-9a-f]{6,}\]?$/ and print a sentence plus the hash as a correlation token.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code — `function errText(e)`, present in 22/22
nodes.antiPattern: `say(sel,'err', e.message)` — presents a memory address to an operator as though it were an explanation. One fix round patched errText on one screen and then found three distinct shapes across the other 21.

nodes.name: action(btnSel, msgSel, rule, input, after) — the mutating-action helper
nodes.rule: Single-flight guard that SAYS it is busy rather than dropping the click, btn.disabled=true (which is also the breadcrumb spinner signal), message cleared BEFORE the call and re-asserted AFTER the reload, try/catch/finally — 18 of 22 components.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code
nodes.antiPattern: Leaving the previous action's message on screen: an operator saw a database error after a stock receipt had actually succeeded, and the obvious reaction is to retry and double-receive.

nodes.name: Never assign className on an element you re-query by class
nodes.rule: `el.className = 'app-msg show ok'` deletes the class the element was FOUND by, so the next q('.<pfx>-msg') returns null and every later message is swallowed in silence; use classList.remove/add on the state tokens only.
nodes.artefact: `function appMsgClass(el, kind)` — 20 of 22 components
nodes.antiPattern: Combined with action()'s clear-before, the wipe happens on the FIRST say of every action and the one carrying the result can never land — an empty, success-styled alert after an HTTP 200 is exactly this line.

nodes.name: data-<pfx>-bound idempotent binding plus one delegated listener
nodes.rule: bind(sel,ev,fn) stamps `data-app-bound` so a render() that runs many times per mount cannot stack listeners, pushes into a BOUND array drained by a ctx.onCleanup registered synchronously at the top, and row actions are delegated on the static tbody because rows are rebuilt every render.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code — `const BOUND = []` in 22/22, `function bind` in 21/22
nodes.antiPattern: Binding the per-row Edit buttons individually: it works on the first draw and then quietly stops, because render() replaced the elements.

nodes.name: "Open source" icon beside every lookup select
nodes.rule: A small icon button (data-manage="<fieldId>") beside each lookup-backed <select> opens the stock CRUD page that maintains that table in a new tab, resolving the URL by stripping this page's own alias off location.pathname; a window `focus` listener reloads the screen on return.
nodes.artefact: properties.html `<span class="<pfx>-field">…<button class="<pfx>-manage" data-manage=…>` + a `<PFX>_MANAGE_URL` map and self-contained IIFE in the script — 13 of 22
nodes.antiPattern: Shipping three working tabs on a screen whose picker has no rows: "there are 3 tabs and I can't find place to input item". Every acceptance test began "given a stock item…" and the step that produces one was owned by no requirement — a fixture is a decision about who creates the row, made silently.

nodes.name: A CSS alias layer in "*", patched by four identical dark blocks
nodes.rule: css.byTheme carries "*" (the full design, :root aliases resolving var(--current-line, <light literal>) etc.) plus Dracula/Forest/Dark/"Dark Blue" blocks of ~644 bytes that redefine ONLY --<pfx>-ok/-warn/-bad/-info/-neutral/-accent, because the platform's --green/--cyan/--purple collapse to one hue on two dark skins and measure 2–3:1 on the card surface.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.css.byTheme — five keys on 22/22; no "Standard" key, the "*" block IS the light design
nodes.antiPattern: Binding status colour to a platform semantic token: on two of the four dark skins green==primary and cyan==pink==purple, so "green = OK / blue = info" silently stops carrying state. Also: five per-skin copies of the WHOLE sheet — patch only the six alias lines.

nodes.name: Flexbox micro-charts — sparkline, meter, week strip, segmented bar
nodes.rule: `<div class="x-sparkbars">` of `<span style="height:N%">` over `display:flex;align-items:flex-end;height:56px` gives a themed sparkline with zero library bytes; the same trick gives a progress meter and an 8-week bucket strip, and style= is used for layout only so 24a's inline-colour rule is respected.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code + css.byTheme["*"]
nodes.antiPattern: Vendoring d3 or echarts for a 12-bar trend indicator, then discovering the library portals its tooltip to document.body where your scoped CSS cannot reach it.

nodes.name: A shell that hosts <plugin> children writes only into empty containers it owns
nodes.rule: The one component containing <plugin> tags keeps every server-rendered chart in Bootstrap row/col cells and every JS-written region in a separate empty `.<pfx>-*` div; there is not one ctx.setHtml, ctx.showHtml or root.innerHTML= in 3 047 nodes, so the "embedded plugin vanishes until a full reload" failure cannot occur.
nodes.artefact: properties.html with `<plugin id="…" name="chart.js.plugin">` siblings + scripts writing only to q('.<pfx>-region')
nodes.antiPattern: ctx.setHtml/showHtml or ctx.include{mode:'replace'} over a container holding a live <plugin>: the DOM goes while Wicket still tracks the component server-side, silently, with no console trace.

nodes.name: row.localize on the wire, plus a <key>Loc repair channel
nodes.rule: The export declares the column as `localized` but the executor renames it to `localize` on every read — read both — and when the jsonb DTO arrives empty a second CRUD returns {rowId, loc} per entity under a `<key>Loc` payload key that appApplyLoc() folds into `<key>` by suffix, so adding a list needs no JS change.
nodes.artefact: `function appLocRaw/appLocList/appMergeLoc/appApplyLoc/locName/dimHuman` — 15–16 of 22 components
nodes.antiPattern: `if (Array.isArray(rows))` on the side channel: the *Loc producers declare returnsArray:false, so a single-row channel is a bare object, arr() returns [] and the merge silently no-ops.

nodes.name: A translate-in-place routine must touch text nodes, never textContent
nodes.rule: `el.textContent = t` on a container is a subtree delete wearing a string assignment — every marker nested inside a translated <label> is destroyed on first draw; walk the element's own child text nodes instead, and restore the authored default from a second attribute so the swap is two-way.
nodes.artefact: `function applyLocale()` over `[data-hy]`/`[data-en]` — 22 of 22, called at the end of every render()
nodes.antiPattern: The whole data-<lang> attribute machine is the anti-pattern 24 §9 names — it exists here only because every rule reads the always-null context.data.localeKey instead of service.global.locale.getKey(), which forced a browser sniff plus an injected `__loc` attr on every call. Fix the rule; keep only setLocale's asymmetry (a default locale is the absence of evidence, not evidence of English).

nodes.name: Self-instrumenting component — a one-shot ctx.callRule wrapper
nodes.rule: An IIFE keeps the original as ctx.__ghLogRaw, guards with ctx.__ghLogWrapped, times every call, writes level/source/action/message/detail/durationMs/url/build to a log rule, skips logging the logger, and injects the reading locale into every input — with the collector rule swallowing its own failures on purpose.
nodes.artefact: studioModel.scripts[].code lines 1–70 of 17 of 22 components + a `Log UI Event (Studio)` EXECUTION rule + a build-stamp div in the markup
nodes.antiPattern: Logging the happy path too: the bridge is a blocking XHR, so a wrapped screen freezes the tab TWICE per action. Log only rejections and ok===false unless actively debugging.

nodes.name: Six classic layout archetypes reused across all four projects
nodes.rule: gen_row_*/gen_slot_* form scaffold; the filter cell `<div class="mb-3"><plugin id="form-label" name="nct.label.plugin"><plugin id="field" name="dynaform.form.*.field.plugin">`; the filter row of parsis slots; the page head (h4 + text-muted small, both label plugins); the dashboard grid (main-card mb-3 card + card-header lnr-* icon + row/col + chart.js.plugin, each chart captioned by a -t title and -s subtitle label); and card/N-col wrappers.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin properties.html (no studioModel) hosting nct.label.plugin / nct.parsis.plugin / dynaform.form.*.field.plugin / chart.js.plugin
nodes.antiPattern: Leaving these nodes' identifiers as raw UUIDs (one project did, for 267 nodes) — the tree becomes unnavigable and a <plugin id> can no longer be read against the node it binds.

nodes.name: Reads are camelCase, writes are snake_case — declare the mapping once
nodes.rule: The executor camelCases every column label on the way out while create/update take the real column names, so one field has three spellings (row key, editor selector, rule input key); keep them side by side in one FIELDS table in the component so they cannot drift.
nodes.artefact: `const FIELDS = [['targetRatePerUnit','#va-rate','targetRate',2], …]` driving both the payload build and the editor fill
nodes.antiPattern: A save that silently drops a field because the patch map key never matched a column — the executor has nothing to complain about. This is also why 21/22 components ship a dual-case pick(o,k) despite 24c saying not to.

nodes.name: Wordless chart + nct.label.plugin heading sibling
nodes.rule:
Strip every word out of the chart (HTML tab = `
`, no `title.text`, `legend:{display:false}` so hard-coded dataset labels never render) and put the caption on a sibling `nct.label.plugin` whose `properties.text` is a LOCALIZED_STRING covering every locale; name those labels `hdr_` so the pairing survives layout edits.
nodes.artefact: chart.js.plugin (properties.Javascript.stringValue) + sibling nct.label.plugin (properties.text, propertyType LOCALIZED_STRING)
nodes.antiPattern: Typing the chart title into the JS tab's title.text or into the HTML tab: renders identically under every locale and no offline gate sees it.

nodes.name: Inline <plugin> + <prop type="LOCALIZED_STRING"> inside html markup
nodes.rule: nct.html.plugin's `html` property is propertyType STRING with a permanently empty localizedStringValue, so never type a word into it: embed a real `<plugin name="nct.label.plugin"><prop name="text" type="LOCALIZED_STRING" value='{"hy_AM":"…","ru_RU":"…","en_US":"…"}'></prop></plugin>` (single-quoted attribute holding GSON of a locale→text map); the alternative is an empty `<plugin id="form-label" name="nct.label.plugin"></plugin>` slot backed by a real child content node.
nodes.artefact: nct.html.plugin → properties.html.stringValue; plugin/prop composition tags
